That creature may immediately make a {@action Devour|lustvore} check on a creature within range, even if that creature isn't {@condition grappled}.

subclassFeature.name: College of the Glutton
entries: Bards of this college desire one thing only: To consume. Usually, food. And people.

Often those that are part of the college of the glutton are natural hedonists: inclined to continue to eat and put on more weight due to their never ending hunger or simple addiction to food (and people!). Some bards of this path will become chefs in an attempt to sate their own desires for delicious treats, but often such a task is time consuming and rarely produces the amount of food required, and thus more often do they simply hire on cooks or use their talents to eat those around them instead!

subclassFeature.name: Belly Casting
entries: At 3rd level, When you join the College of the Glutton you may use your gut as your spellcasting focus, and all verbal components of spells may be replaced with loud gastrointestinal noises.

subclassFeature.name: Immense Appetite
entries: At 3rd level, you increase your capacity as if you were one size larger.

subclassFeature.name: Selfish Hunger
entries: At 3rd level, you focus your gluttonous desires inwards. Once per turn, during any point when you take the {@action Devour|lustvore} action, you may expend a use of your Bardic Inspiration on yourself to do one of the following:

items: {@i {@b Gulp.}} You gain one additional success on an ongoing devour contest where you are predator. This upgrades to 2 successes at 14th level.
{@i {@b Growl.}} You add your Bardic Inspiration die to your devour roll. This may be done after seeing the result of yours and the enemies rolls.

{@i {@b Gurgle.}} You add your Bardic Inspiration die to your digestion damage this turn, and regain hit points equal to the roll on your Bardic Inspiration die + your Constitution modifier. You may do this as a bonus action anytime instead of during a {@action Devour|lustvore} action.

subclassFeature.name: Extra Attack
entries: Starting at 6th level, you can attack twice, instead of once, whenever you take the {@action Attack} action on your turn.

subclassFeature.name: Devouring Spell
entries: Starting at 14th level, when you use your action to cast a spell, or whenever you expend a Bardic Inspiration, you can make a {@action Devour|lustvore} check as a bonus action without needing to grapple your target first.

subclassFeature.name: Gluttony Domain
entries: The gods of the new world embody the hope of the many- peace, justice, agriculture and creation. However, some gods revel in ancient tradition born of sacrifice and hedonism. Yours is one such god- one that promotes gluttony above all else. Followers obey a ravenous doctrine- to consume, to amass, and to spread the hunger so that all may revel in its grand excess.

subclassFeature.name: Body Expertise
entries: Starting at 1st level, choose either {@skill Athletics} or {@skill Acrobatics}. You are now proficient in your chosen skill, and your Proficiency Bonus is doubled for any ability check you make that uses your chosen skill.

entries.caption: Gluttony Domain Spells
rows: 1st
{@spell intensify hunger|lustvore}, {@spell flavor/disgust|lustvore}
3rd
{@spell sophie's ravenous consumption|lustvore}, {@spell devouring smite|lustvore}
5th
{@spell greater belch|lustvore}, {@spell maddening hunger|lustvore}
7th
{@spell leeching insides|lustvore}, {@spell entice|lustvore}
9th
{@spell bellyport|lustvore}, {@spell inhale|lustvore}

subclassFeature.name: Ravenous Blessing
entries: Starting when you choose this domain at 1st level, you can awaken the latent hunger in a creature with your touch. You can touch a creature as an action. For the next minute, that creature may use their bonus action for a single {@action devour|lustvore} attack.
You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier (a minimum of once). You regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

subclassFeature.name: Channel Divinity: Divine Feast
entries: Starting at 2nd level, you can use your Channel Divinity to invoke a grand feast in the name of gluttony. As an action, you may present your holy symbol. You and any allies within 30 feet that can see or hear you may use their reaction to move up to their move speed. As part of the same reaction, they can attempt to {@action Devour|lustvore} a creature without needing to grapple them first.

subclassFeature.name: Glutton's Reward
entries: At 6th level, your divine powers reward excess and gluttony. When you cast a spell that would restore hit points to a creature, that creature gains temporary hit points equal to the total capacity points of creatures and food they contain. A creature can never gain more than ½ their maximum health in temporary hit points in this manner, and any temporary hit points gained exceeding ½ their maximum health are lost.

subclassFeature.name: Extra Attack
entries: Starting at 8th level, you can attack twice, instead of once, whenever you take the {@action Attack} action on your turn.

subclassFeature.name: Aura of Excess
entries: Starting at 17th level, you can use your action to activate an aura of gluttony and hunger that radiates out from you in a 30 foot radius. Creatures of your choice within that radius must make a Wisdom saving throw or be {@condition charmed} by you for one minute. At the start of their turns, creatures {@condition charmed} in this way will use their action to make {@action Grapple} and {@action Devour|lustvore} attacks against the closest target within reach, determined randomly. If there are no targets within reach, they must use their movement to move towards the nearest valid target. They may roll the saving throw again whenever they successfully swallow a creature.
Once you use this feature you may not do so again until you finish a long rest.

subclassFeature.name: Gutslut Domain
entries: There are those prey out there that regard the experience of being trapped inside another creature as euphoric… Divine even. Those that pursue these preyish tendencies begin to regard it as a form of worship, eschewing other pleasures and activities in favor of squeezing guts and teasing predators. And from their love and pleasure was born the Gutslut Domain, resonating with all those that seek their similar desires…

There is no formal name for this domain. Some simply call it a portion of the domain of pleasure. Some call it the domain of stomachs. Some decry it's even existence, merely proclaiming it to be an illusion brought on by lack of oxygen in the stomach. A hundred and one words exist for it. Yet no matter the name, they all practice their worship through one thing: Climbing down the throat of the nearest and most enticing predator and worshipping their belly as their own personal church, and leaving their fate in the hands of their predators.

Perhaps because of these preyish tendencies that it's exceedingly rare to encounter a cleric of these domains. Most often they are digested early on in their career, or perpetually kept inside another creature's gut as an unknown bulge.

But those that survive for long enough learn to become one with their predator in body and soul, finally reaching those heightened pinnacles to be rewarded with living out their fantasies over and over and over… And their predators are rewarded with the power to keep them inside forever…

entries.caption: Gutslut Domain Spells
rows: 1st
{@spell cure wounds}, {@spell flavor/disgust|lustvore}
3rd
{@spell homunculi food|lustvore}, {@spell healing massage|lustvore}
5th
{@spell medicinal acids|lustvore}, {@spell meal of the phoenix|lustvore}
7th
{@spell bellypot ally|lustvore}, {@spell entice|lustvore}
9th
{@spell belly fortune telling|lustvore}, {@spell greater restoration}

subclassFeature.name: A Gutsluts Purpose
entries: At 1st level, While you are inside another creature, when you normally would roll one or more dice to restore hit points, you instead roll the highest number possible when restoring hit points to solely your predator. This has no effect for effects that restore or create temporary hit points.

In addition you are able to cast spells as if you were standing in the predator's square without the {@condition swallowed|lustvore} condition, as you channel the magic through their eyes and body. And you no longer need to make {@status concentration} checks when attempting to cast spells while inside a stomach that has not dealt digestion damage to you since the end of your last turn, and you have advantage on {@status concentration} checks while you are inside a belly even if it has dealt damage to you.

subclassFeature.name: Eternal Meal
entries: At 1st level, through a one hour intimate ritual involving yourself and your predator of your choice, you pledge yourself to be their Eternal Meal.

Whenever you are digested, if your predator is alive, you return to the body of your chosen predator upon their next short or long rest, counting as if you had just had a short or long rest respectively. This ability does not function if your soul is bound, such as being absorbed, trapped, etc.
You can recast this ritual once per day to select a new predator, replacing your old one.
In addition, you are more often targeted by hungry predators due to your inherent prey nature.

subclassFeature.name: Channel Divinity: Gutsluts Promise
entries: Starting at 2nd level, you can use your channel divinity to cry out in bliss about your state and empower your predator with the strength of their squeezing insides.

As an action you throw yourself at the mercy of your predator's gut. While this is active, your let your predators guts use you as a meal for strength, dealing damage equal to 5 + twice your level at the end of your turn that ignores all resistances and immunities. During this time, they gain your Proficiency Bonus as a bonus to all attack rolls and damage rolls, skill checks, and saving throws. This continues until you expend a bonus action to cancel it, or until you are {@condition defeated|lustvore}/{@condition unconscious}/killed.
This does count as digestion damage for the purpose of Divine Feast.

subclassFeature.name: Divine Feast
entries: At 6th level, your body becomes an impossibly nutritious snack, allowing predators to sap your strength to heal their bodies. Whenever your predator deals digestion damage against you, they gain that much hit points restored to them. If they are at max or if it would exceed max, it becomes temporary hit points.

Upon reaching 0 hit points or lower through digestion damage, roll a {@status concentration} saving throw vs DC 10 or the digestion damage dealt, whichever is higher. On a success, you are not {@condition defeated|lustvore} and return to 1 hit point. All damage done beyond 0 hit points is not counted for purposes of restoring health to the predator.

subclassFeature.name: Bonded Gutslut
entries: At 8th level, you learn how to infuse your predator with power. You gain the following abilities:

items: {@i {@b Infuse Courage:}} As an action, you can cause your predator to reroll the saving throw to break out of an ongoing spell or effect, such as {@condition frightened}, {@condition charmed}, {@spell command}, etc. This saving throw roll is done with advantage.

{@i {@b Infuse Hunger:}} As an action, you can cause your predator to feel extreme pangs of hunger. The predator can take a {@action grapple} or {@action devour|LustVore} action against a creature in reach as a reaction.

{@i {@b Infuse Pleasure:}} As an action, you can give pleasure to your predator to mask the pain. They gain temporary hit points equal to your Cleric level + Wisdom modifier, that lasts so long as you are inside them.

{@i {@b Infuse Protection:}} As an action, you can give protection to your predator. They gain +2 to their armor class and stomach AC until the end of your next turn. This upgrades to +4 at 14th level.

{@i {@b Infuse Strength:}} As an action, you can give strength to your predator. They gain an additional {@dice 1d8} radiant damage to their weapons and unarmed attacks until the end of your next turn. This upgrades to {@dice 2d8} at 14th level.

subclassFeature.name: Gut Magnetism
entries: At 17th level, you are so drawn to predators that you are able to pledge yourself to them with but a plea of desire.

You may select a new predator to become bonded with for your Eternal Meal. The predator no longer needs to be {@condition willing|lustvore}. As part of the same action, you teleport yourself into their belly per the {@spell bellyport ally|lustvore} spell, cast at your spell save DC if needed.
You may use this ability once per short or long rest.

subclassFeature.name: Pleasure Domain
entries: You have pledged yourself to the pleasure domain, seeking out pleasure and bringing it to friends and foes alike.

entries.caption: Pleasure Domain Spells
rows: 1st
{@spell share sensation|lustvore}, {@spell vision of exquisite pleasure|lustvore}
3rd
{@spell disrobe|lustvore}, {@spell enhance ability}
5th
{@spell promise of pleasure|lustvore}, {@spell orgasmic vibrations|lustvore}
7th
{@spell aura of lust|lustvore}, {@spell evard's black tentacles}
9th
{@spell come to me|lustvore}, {@spell hold monster}

subclassFeature.name: Unarmored Defense
entries: At 1st level, you learn how to shed your armor to get closer to those around you. You gain an armor class equal to 10 + your Dexterity modifier + your Wisdom modifier.

subclassFeature.name: Channel Divinity: Enticing Beauty
entries: Starting at 2nd level, you can use your channel divinity to entice others to join you in pleasure.

As an action, you may present your {@item holy symbol|phb}, and each creature of your choice within 30 feet must make a Wisdom saving throw. On a failure, they are {@condition charmed} until the end of your next turn or until they take any damage. You can also command them to approach you during their turn when they fail the saving throw.

subclassFeature.name: Touch of Ecstasy
entries: At 6th level, you learn how to overwhelm your opponents with pleasure. When you make an attack that deals lewd damage, you can force one damaged enemy to make a Charisma saving throw. On a failure, they are {@condition stunned} until the end of their next turn.
You may do this a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier and regain all uses on a long rest.

subclassFeature.name: Divine Strike
entries: At 8th level, once on each of your turns when you hit a creature with a weapon attack or unarmed attack, you can cause the attack to deal an extra {@dice 1d8} lewd damage to the target. When you reach 14th level, the extra damage increases to {@dice 2d8}.

subclassFeature.name: Moment of Rapture
entries: At 17th level, you are able to grant anyone a rapturous orgasm. When you use your Touch of Ecstasy feature, creatures that fail the save are now {@condition paralyzed} until the end of their next turn rather than {@condition stunned}. This counts as them orgasming for the purpose of various spells and effects.

subclassFeature.name: Circle of the Chimera
entries: The Circle of the Chimera are druids who have chosen to keep their original forms, but improve upon it with the best features of the creatures they know and consume. For many, it's considered a right of passage to hunt and digest a creature before they use their powers, even if they could learn it from another source.
Those Druids that practice the circle of the Chimera are often predators themselves, but it's not unknown to be prey as well.

subclassFeature.name: Body Expertise
entries: Starting at 2nd level, choose either {@skill Athletics} or {@skill Acrobatics}. You are now proficient in your chosen skill, and your Proficiency Bonus is doubled for any ability check you make that uses your chosen skill.

subclassFeature.name: Chimera Forms
entries: Starting at 2nd level, you gain the ability to partially change your physiology, granting you the traits of various animals. You are no longer able to wild shape into animals.
Instead, as an action or bonus action, you can expend a use of your Wild Shape feature in order to gain two of the following effects, until you use this feature again:

items: {@b Bear's Teeth:} You gain a new natural weapon attack that you are considered proficient in, bite: This attack deals 1d10 + Strength modifier piercing damage.
{@b Beetle's Armor:} Your Base AC becomes equal to 13 + your Wisdom modifier.
{@b Cheetah's Legs:} Your movement speed increases by 10 feet.
{@b Crocodile's Maw:} During a {@action devour|lustvore} contest, creatures have disadvantage on escape actions. This does not include resisting being devoured.
{@b Eagle's Eyes:} You gain advantage on {@skill Perception} and {@skill Insight} checks.
{@b Fish Fins:} You gain a swimming speed equal to your movement speed.

{@b Frog's Tongue:} You may make {@action grapple} attempts on creatures up to 15 feet away. On a success, you pull them adjacent. If you are able to {@action devour|lustvore} without grappling, you are able to do the same with {@action devour|lustvore} attempts.

{@b Gazelle’s Hooves:} When you successfully avoid a {@action grapple} or {@action devour|lustvore} contest as a prey and your speed is not 0, you can use your reaction to instantly move ½ your movement without provoking attacks of opportunity.
{@b Rat Instincts:} You gain advantage on {@skill Survival} checks, a sixth sense for danger, and cannot be {@status surprised}.
{@b Snake's Jaw:} You gain advantage on {@action devour|lustvore} contests as a predator against creatures of a smaller size.

entries: This feature follows the normal rules for the time limit per standard Wild Shape, but none of the other restrictions of Wild Shape. This feature upgrades to 3 effects at 4th level, and 4 effects at 8th level

subclassFeature.name: Extra Attack
entries: Starting at 6th level, you can attack twice, instead of once, whenever you take the {@action Attack} action on your turn.

subclassFeature.name: Monstrous Chimera Form
entries: Starting at 10th level, the following options are added to your chimera form features as possible options:

items: {@b Bulette's Mandibles:} You gain a burrow speed equal to half your movement speed.
{@b Displacer Beast's Pelt:} The first attack each turn that targets you is made with disadvantage.
{@b Froghemoth's Gut:} You count as one size larger for the purpose of determining capacity.
{@b Harpy's Wings:} You gain a flying speed equal to your movement speed.

{@b Manticore's Tail:} You now gain a tail (if you didn’t have one already) and tail maw that is able to count as an additional hand for grappling, and an additional orifice for {@condition devouring|lustvore}. You can take a bonus action {@action devour|lustvore} with disadvantage using your tail maw against a target you have not already targeted during your turn with a devour check. This target does not need to be {@condition grappled} first. This test is no longer done at disadvantage if you already have 1 or more devour contest success.

{@b Ogre's Acids:} You can now digest anything except for magical items and artifacts. All creatures and objects inside you that have immunity to digestion become resistant, and all creatures that had resistance to digestion lose their resistances.
{@b Trapper's Flesh:} You gain advantage on {@skill Stealth} checks, and can hide when lightly obscured.
{@b Troll's Regeneration:} You regain 4 hit points at the start of your turn while you are above 0 hit points.
{@b Yeti's Strength:} You gain advantage on Strength checks and saving throws.

subclassFeature.name: Fluid Chimera Form
entries: Starting at 14th level, while you are in your chimera form, you may use your bonus action to lose one of your effects, and replace it with any other effect you have not already chosen.

subclassFeature.name: Circle of the Dryad
entries: A circle of the Dryad druid takes a more focused approach than many other of their druid kin. Where most druids focus on plants as a whole, Circle of the Dryad Druids are more focused on plant life. They resonate with trees, flowers, and the very earth itself.

subclassFeature.name: Botanical Growth
entries: At 2nd level, you are able to shape nature to your whims. As an action, you can expend a use of your Wild Shape feature to activate Botanical Growth:

items: From your body you sprout one large winding vine. This increases to 2 vines a 4th level, and 3 vines at 8th level. These vines last for one hour, or until you dismiss them as an action.

When you use Botanical Growth, you can make an {@action attack}, {@action grapple}, or {@action shove} attack with each vine. You may use your vines again as your action on any turn while your vines last.

These vines have a 15 feet, and use your spellcasting attack modifier for {@action attack||attacks}, {@action grapple||grapples}, and {@action shove||shoves}. On successful attack, they deal {@dice 1d8} + your Wisdom modifier bludgeoning damage.

A vine that has a creature {@condition grappled} cannot attack or target creatures other than the {@condition grappled} creature. Each vine can only grapple one creature at a time. Vines can drag {@condition grappled} creatures up to 15 feet as their action. If you ever move out of your vine's reach when they have a creature {@condition grappled}, the grapple breaks instantly.

subclassFeature.name: Soul of the Dryad
entries: At 2nd level, you are able to commune with plants. You know the {@spell speak with plants} spell, and casting it does not use up a spellslot. You may use this feature a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier per long rest.

subclassFeature.name: Botanical Infusions
entries: At 6th level, you learn how to infuse your plant growth with special abilities. When you activate your Botanical Growth feature, you may now select one botanical infusion from the list below for your vines. These botanical infusions may not be changed once chosen unless you expend another use of the wild shape feature.

items: {@b Alluring Scent:} Your vine emits a particularly alluring aphrodisiac that dampens a creature's will to resist. When this vine has a target {@condition grappled} they suffer disadvantage on all Strength and Dexterity checks.

{@b Bark Shield:} Your vines grow thick and tough. When you take an action to use your vines, you may instead use your vines to provide +3 AC to a creature in range of the vine until the end of your next turn.
{@b Nature's Reach:} Your vines now have a reach of 60 feet.

{@b Pleasurable Textures:} Your vines grow a soft and pleasurably smooth texture. This vine deals {@dice 2d6} + your Wisdom modifier lewd damage when attacking {@condition grappled}, {@condition restrained}, and {@condition prone} targets, and may choose to deal lewd damage instead of its normal damage types.

{@b Predatory Plant Growth:} Your vines resemble some type of predatory plant, such as a venus flytrap or a pitcher plant. When you use an action to use your vines, you may instead use your vines to make a {@action devour|lustvore} check against a creature they have {@condition grappled}.

subclassFeature.name: One With Nature
entries: At 10th level, you are able to call upon the forest and sprout a beautiful grove that’s under your control.

As an action, you are suddenly engulfed in a plant-cocoon, and a beautiful fantastical grove sprouts in a 120 feet radius around you. Your cocoon may take any shape you wish, such as a flower, a tree, the belly of a dryad, and so forth, but remains stationary and visible in the center.
If you activate this inside another creature, your vines sprout from their body and pin them to the ground. They have a speed of 0 and cannot be moved or pushed against their will.
This plant cocoon has 4 hit points for every level you have in this class. While in this cocoon, your speed is reduced to 0, and you cannot be pushed or moved against your will.
The grove around you is considered difficult terrain for any creatures of your choice as nature herself works to impede their progress.
If the cocoon ever falls to 0 hit points, you are knocked out of the cocoon. The grove remains, although may wither and die if it is in an inhospitable environment.
You may activate this ability once per long rest.

subclassFeature.name: Improved Botanical Infusions
entries: At 14th level, when you use Botanical Growth, you may choose two botanical infusions instead of one.

subclassFeature.name: Circle of the Shepherd
entries: Druids of the Circle of the Shepherd commune with the spirits of nature, especially the spirits of beasts and the fey, and call to those spirits for aid. These druids recognize that all living things play a role in the natural world, yet they focus on protecting animals and fey creatures that have difficulty defending themselves. Shepherds, as they are known, see such creatures as their charges. They ward off monsters that threaten them, rebuke hunters who kill more prey than necessary, and prevent civilization from encroaching on rare animal habitats and on sites sacred to the fey. Many of these druids are happiest far from cities and towns, content to spend their days in the company of animals and the fey creatures of the wilds.

Members of this circle become adventurers to oppose forces that threaten their charges or to seek knowledge and power that will help them safeguard their charges better. Wherever these druids go, the spirits of the wilderness are with them.

subclassFeature.name: Speech of the Woods
entries: At 2nd level, you gain the ability to converse with beasts and many fey.

You learn to speak, read, and write {@language Sylvan}. In addition, beasts can understand your speech, and you gain the ability to decipher their noises and motions. Most beasts lack the intelligence to convey or understand sophisticated concepts, but a friendly beast could relay what it has seen or heard in the recent past. This ability doesn't grant you friendship with beasts, though you can combine this ability with gifts to curry favor with them as you would with any nonplayer character.

subclassFeature.name: Spirit Totem
entries: Starting at 2nd level, you can call forth nature spirits to influence the world around you. As a bonus action, you can magically summon an incorporeal spirit to a point you can see within 60 feet of you. The spirit creates an aura in a 30-foot radius around that point. It counts as neither a creature nor an object, though it has the spectral appearance of the creature it represents.
As a bonus action, you can move the spirit up to 60 feet to a point you can see.
The spirit persists for 1 minute or until you're {@condition incapacitated}. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a short or long rest.
The effect of the spirit's aura depends on the type of spirit you summon from the options below.

entries.name: Bear Spirit
entries: The bear spirit grants you and your allies its might and endurance. Each creature of your choice in the aura when the spirit appears gains temporary hit points equal to 5 + your druid level. In addition, you and your allies gain advantage on Strength checks and Strength saving throws while in the aura.

entries.name: Hawk Spirit
entries: The hawk spirit is a consummate hunter, aiding you and your allies with its keen sight. When a creature makes an attack roll against a target in the spirit's aura, you can use your reaction to grant advantage to that attack roll. In addition, you and your allies have advantage on Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) checks while in the aura.

entries.name: Unicorn Spirit
entries: The unicorn spirit lends its protection to those nearby. You and your allies gain advantage on all ability checks made to detect creatures in the spirit's aura. In addition, if you cast a spell using a spell slot that restores hit points to any creature inside or outside the aura, each creature of your choice in the aura also regains hit points equal to your druid level.

subclassFeature.name: Mighty Summoner
entries: Starting at 6th level, beasts and fey that you conjure are more resilient than normal. Any beast or fey summoned or created by a spell that you cast gains the following benefits:

items: The creature appears with more hit points than normal: 2 extra hit points per Hit Die it has. {@b If the summoned creature has no Hit Die, divide the creature's health by the amount it gains per additional spell level to determine how many Hit Die it is considered to have for this feature.}
The damage from its {@b attacks} is considered magical for the purpose of overcoming immunity and resistance to nonmagical attacks and damage.

subclassFeature.name: Guardian Spirit
entries: Beginning at 10th level, your Spirit Totem safeguards the beasts and fey that you call forth with your magic. When a beast or fey that you summoned or created with a spell ends its turn in your Spirit Totem aura, that creature regains a number of hit points equal to half your druid level.

subclassFeature.name: Faithful Summons
entries: Starting at 14th level, the nature spirits you commune with protect you when you are the most defenseless. If you are reduced to 0 hit points or are {@condition incapacitated} against your will, you can immediately gain the benefits of {@spell conjure animals} as if it were cast using a 9th-level spell slot. It summons four beasts of your choice that are challenge rating 2 or lower. The conjured beasts appear within 20 feet of you. If they receive no commands from you, they protect you from harm and attack your foes. The spell lasts for 1 hour, requiring no {@status concentration}, or until you dismiss it (no action required).
Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a long rest.

subclassFeature.name: Battle Master
entries: Those who emulate the archetypal Battle Master employ martial techniques passed down through generations. To a Battle Master, combat is an academic field, sometimes including subjects beyond battle such as weaponsmithing and calligraphy. Not every fighter absorbs the lessons of history, theory, and artistry that are reflected in the Battle Master archetype, but those who do are well-rounded fighters of great skill and knowledge.

subclassFeature.name: Combat Superiority
entries: When you choose this archetype at 3rd level, you learn maneuvers that are fueled by special dice called superiority dice.

entries.name: Maneuvers
entries: You learn three maneuvers of your choice, which are listed under "Maneuvers" below. Many maneuvers enhance an attack in some way. You can use only one maneuver per attack.
You learn two additional maneuvers of your choice at 7th, 10th, and 15th level. Each time you learn new maneuvers, you can also replace one maneuver you know with a different one.

entries.name: Superiority Dice
entries: You have four superiority dice, which are {@dice d8}s. A superiority die is expended when you use it. You regain all of your expended superiority dice when you finish a short or long rest.
You gain another superiority die at 7th level and one more at 15th level.

entries.name: Saving Throws
entries: Some of your maneuvers require your target to make a saving throw to resist the maneuver's effects. The saving throw DC is calculated as follows:

subclassFeature.name: Maneuver Options
entries: {@i 3rd-level fighter {@variantrule optional class features|tce|optional feature}}

If you have access to maneuvers, the following maneuvers are added to the list of options available to you. Maneuvers are available to Battle Masters but also to characters who have a special feature like the {@optfeature Superior Technique|TCE} fighting style or the {@feat Martial Adept} feat.

subclassFeature.name: Maneuvers
entries: The maneuvers are presented in alphabetical order.

subclassFeature.name: Student of War
entries: At 3rd level, you gain proficiency with one type of {@filter artisan's tools|items|source=phb|miscellaneous=mundane|type=artisan's tools} of your choice.

subclassFeature.name: Additional Maneuvers
entries: At 7th level, you learn two additional maneuvers of your choice.

subclassFeature.name: Additional Superiority Die
entries: You gain another superiority die at 7th level.

subclassFeature.name: Know Your Enemy
entries: If you spend at least 1 minute observing or interacting with another creature outside combat, you can learn certain information about its capabilities compared to your own. The DM tells you if the creature is your equal, superior, or inferior in regard to two of the following characteristics of your choice:

items: Strength score
Dexterity score
Constitution score
Armor Class
Current hit points
Total class levels (if any)
Fighter class levels (if any)

subclassFeature.name: Additional Maneuvers
entries: At 10th level, you learn two additional maneuvers of your choice.

subclassFeature.name: Improved Combat Superiority (d10)
entries: At 10th level, your superiority dice turn into {@dice d10}s.

subclassFeature.name: Additional Maneuvers
entries: At 15th level, you learn two additional maneuvers of your choice.

subclassFeature.name: Additional Superiority Die
entries: You gain another superiority die at 15th level.

subclassFeature.name: Relentless
entries: Starting at 15th level, when you roll initiative and have no superiority dice remaining, you regain 1 superiority die.

subclassFeature.name: Improved Combat Superiority (d12)
entries: At 18th level, your superiority dice turn into {@dice d12}s.

subclassFeature.name: Arcane Archer
entries: An Arcane Archer studies a unique elven method of archery that weaves magic into attacks to produce supernatural effects. Arcane Archers are some of the most elite warriors among the elves. They stand watch over the fringes of elven domains, keeping a keen eye out for trespassers and using magic-infused arrows to defeat monsters and invaders before they can reach elven settlements. Over the centuries, the methods of these elf archers have been learned by members of other races who can also balance arcane aptitude with archery.

subclassFeature.name: Arcane Archer Lore
entries: At 3rd level, you learn magical theory or some of the secrets of nature—typical for practitioners of this elven martial tradition. You choose to gain proficiency in either the {@skill Arcana} or the {@skill Nature} skill, and you choose to learn either the {@spell prestidigitation} or the {@spell druidcraft} cantrip.

subclassFeature.name: Arcane Shot
entries: At 3rd level, you learn to unleash special magical effects with some of your shots. When you gain this feature, you learn two Arcane Shot options of your choice (see "Arcane Shot Options" below).

Once per turn when you fire an arrow from a shortbow or longbow as part of the {@action Attack} action, you can apply one of your Arcane Shot options to that arrow. You decide to use the option when the arrow hits a creature, unless the option doesn't involve an attack roll. You have two uses of this ability, and you regain all expended uses of it when you finish a short or long rest.
You gain an additional Arcane Shot option of your choice when you reach certain levels in this class: 7th, 10th, 15th, and 18th level. Each option also improves when you become an 18th-level fighter.
Whenever you gain an additional Arcane Shot option (at 7th, 10th, 15th, and 18th level) you gain an additional use of your Arcane Shot feature.

subclassFeature.name: Arcane Shot Options
entries: The Arcane Shot feature lets you choose options for it at certain levels. The options are presented here in alphabetical order. They are all magical effects, and each one is associated with one of the schools of magic.
If an option requires a saving throw, your Arcane Shot save DC is calculated as follows:

subclassFeature.name: Additional Arcane Shot Option
entries: You gain an additional Arcane Shot option of your choice when you reach 7th level.

subclassFeature.name: Curving Shot
entries: At 7th level, you learn how to direct an errant arrow toward a new target. When you make an attack roll with a magic arrow and miss, you can use a bonus action to reroll the attack roll against a different target within 60 feet of the original target.

subclassFeature.name: Magic Arrow
entries: At 7th level, you gain the ability to infuse arrows with magic. Whenever you fire a nonmagical arrow from a shortbow or longbow, you can make it magical for the purpose of overcoming resistance and immunity to nonmagical attacks and damage. The magic fades from the arrow immediately after it hits or misses its target.

subclassFeature.name: Additional Arcane Shot Option
entries: You gain an additional Arcane Shot option of your choice when you reach 10th level.

subclassFeature.name: Additional Arcane Shot Option
entries: You gain an additional Arcane Shot option of your choice when you reach 15th level.

subclassFeature.name: Ever-Ready Shot
entries: Starting at 15th level, your magical archery is available whenever battle starts. If you roll initiative and have no uses of Arcane Shot remaining, you regain one use of it.

subclassFeature.name: Additional Arcane Shot Option
entries: You gain an additional Arcane Shot option of your choice when you reach 18th level. Each option also improves when you become an 18th-level fighter.

subclassFeature.name: Dominatrix
entries: You are a predator for one reason: Control. You are the queen bee, the alpha, the top bitch in any room, and you ensure that everyone knows it. Your whims might as well be law, and your body a divine temple that they will worship.

subclassFeature.name: Whips and Chains
entries: At 3rd level, you gain proficiency in chains, rope, and other binding equipment as weapons. When you attack with a whip, a chain, rope, or unarmed (lewd or normal), You may deal lewd damage instead of normal damage. If your binding does not have stats for it, it uses your Strength modifier to attack and deals {@damage 1d6} + Strength modifier bludgeoning damage.

In addition, as an attack, you can use a whip, rope, or chain to {@action grapple} foes up to 30 feet away (so long as you have a sufficiently long whip, rope, or chain). On a successful {@action grapple}, they remain at their current distance. You may make contested grappling checks as attacks, each successful one dragging the creature 15 feet closer towards you.
You gain a Dominatrix DC, which is equal to 8 + your Charisma modifier + Proficiency Bonus.

subclassFeature.name: Conjure Binding
entries: At 3rd level, you are able to conjure magical chains, tentacles, rope, or other bindings from the ether to bind around your foes. You can have up to a maximum of two chains that reach up to a maximum of 30 feet. This upgrades to 3 chains at 7th level, and 4 chains at 15th level.

As an action, you may use each chain to choose a target creature. They must make a Dexterity saving throw vs your Dominatrix DC or become bound for 1 minute. They may spend an action to attempt to free themselves with a Dexterity or Strength saving throw vs your Dominatrix DC.

While a creature is affected by your bindings, they are considered {@condition grappled}. However, when you move while binding creature, you can move yourself and not them, as long as you don’t go further than your chain’s maximum range.
While a creature is binded, you may do the following abilities in place of your attacks:

{@b {@i Pull:}} When you take the {@action attack} action, in place of an attack you can make a contested {@action grapple} check. On success, you may pull a binded target up to your maximum chain length closer to you. If your target is two sizes larger than you, you are pulled towards them instead.

{@b {@i Fling:}} When you take the {@action attack} action, in place of an attack you can push a binded target up to 30 feet away. If thrown to the maximum chain length away, you may release your binding on them to fling them up to 20 feet in additional distance away. If you release them, they must make a Dexterity saving throw or suffer {@dice 1d6} bludgeoning damage for every 10 feet thrown AFTER they are released from the chain or half on a success. Hitting a wall or another creature deals an additional {@dice 2d6} bludgeoning damage to both the thrown creature and the creature they collide with; the hit creature also gets to make the Dexterity saving throw as well to halve the damage. This damage is done in place of normal fall damage.

subclassFeature.name: Holding Cell
entries: At 7th level, your gut is your own personal cell, allowing you to toy with your victims for as long as you desire. You gain the following effects:

items: Instead of dealing digestion damage to any creatures inside you, you can choose to force all creatures inside of you to make a Constitution saving throw versus your Dominatrix DC, on fail they are {@condition incapacitated} until the end of their next turn. If a creature inside of you was targeted by an attack, spell, or other ability on your turn, they have advantage on the saving throw. Outside of combat you can declare you're doing this ability indefinitely.
While inside your body, your prey never needs to eat or drink.

You may choose to make any number of creatures inside you immune to your digestion as a free action and may retract it just as easily. Gear does not count as part of a creature (and thus may be digested separately).
You treat your capacity as one size larger.

subclassFeature.name: Submission
entries: At 10th level, While a creature is affected by your chain's ability, you can force them to submit. You may use an action to target a creature binded by you: They must roll a Wisdom saving throw vs your Dominatrix DC or be {@condition charmed}. While they are {@condition charmed}, they realize resistance is futile and will stop fighting you and your allies if they were prior. In addition, reluctantly or otherwise, they will respond to any commands you give it, so long as the command is not clearly suicidal or doing something strongly against its nature, such as attacking its friends. This charm lasts for as long as they remain affected by your binding ability, attached to you such as being on a roped collar, or within 10 feet of you (or inside you!). They may roll to break free of this every time they take damage or are commanded to do something strongly against its nature. (even though they don’t need to follow the command if they fail).
You may use this ability once per long rest.

subclassFeature.name: Improved Chains
entries: At 15th level, when you use your conjure binding ability to fling or pull a creature, you may target all bound creatures with the attack.

subclassFeature.name: Devoted Following
entries: At 18th level when you charm a {@condition defeated|lustvore} creature using your submission ability, they become completely and utterly devoted to you, as they regard you as a living goddess or god. Once {@condition charmed} by your submission ability, a creature remains permanently {@condition charmed} and remains in effect even after they leave your side. They will follow any command you give them, including suicidal ones, and the charm remains in effect permanently unless broken by abilities and spells that can negate charm conditions, or you are {@condition defeated|lustvore}, knocked {@condition unconscious}, or killed in combat with a hostile enemy.

subclassFeature.name: Entrapper
entries: Many predators see consumed prey as little more than food to be churned up for their personal pleasure and sustenance. However there are those who see digestion as more of an unfortunate side effect to the true advantage of devourment: The ability to trap and control their enemies (and friends!), to lord over other creatures in their stomach and make their whole world revolve around their existence in their slimy guts.

To this, many professions on the fringes of civilization often use vore as a means of control. Bounty hunters, prison wardens, kidnappers, and so on. Other professions find use in the ability to store precious people and objects in their bodies for long journeys and emerging unharmed, like merchants and bodyguards. It’s even rumored that great lords and ladies will sometimes choose the safety and privacy of riding in a trusted warriors belly than a carriage.
These entrappers use their strong frames and bodies to their advantage, specializing in grappling arts that allow them to control their enemies just as much outside of their bodies as within.

subclassFeature.name: Pinning Techniques
entries: At 3rd level, you’ve learned the best way to control your foes is through your strong hands and strong gut. You’ve learned the following techniques:

items: Your unarmed strikes now deal {@damage 1d4} + Strength modifier bludgeoning damage, and you now have a new natural melee weapon attack that you are proficient in, {@b {@i Pin.}} This attack can only be used against creatures you have {@condition grappled}, {@condition devouring|lustvore|swallowing}, or {@condition swallowed|lustvore}, and on a hit deals {@damage 2d6} + Strength modifier bludgeoning damage.
You have advantage on attack rolls against creatures you are {@condition grappled||grappling}

In place of one of your attacks, you may attempt to restrain a creature you have {@condition grappled} by making another {@action grapple} check. If you succeed, the creature is {@condition restrained} until the {@action grapple} ends.
Whenever you are able to make an Attack of opportunity, you may attempt a single grapple instead.

As a bonus action, you may deal {@damage 1d4} + Strength modifier bludgeoning damage against one creature you have {@condition grappled}, {@condition devouring|lustvore|swallowing}, or {@condition swallowed|lustvore}.

subclassFeature.name: Walking Jail
entries: At 3rd level, you are able to keep your prey alive for as long as you wish and keep them down more effectively. You gain the following effects:

items: While inside your body, your prey never needs to eat or drink.

You may choose to make any number of creatures inside you immune to your digestion as a free action and may retract it just as easily. Gear does not count as part of a creature (and thus may be digested separately).
While you are filled with at least half your capacity in living creatures, you are considered fed.
You treat your capacity as one size larger.
You increase your stomach AC by +2

subclassFeature.name: Mobile Storage
entries: At 7th level, you learn how to fill yourself even more, and use your prey to help contain and protect them. You no longer suffer movement penalties from being over capacity and attacks no longer have advantage against you.

In addition, you are no longer considered {@condition restrained} when you are over maximum capacity. Instead you move at ½ speed, you have disadvantage on {@skill Stealth} and {@skill Acrobatics} checks, as well as Dexterity saving throws, and all attacks against you gain advantage.

subclassFeature.name: Iron Grip
entries: At 10th level, your control over your opponents is masterful.

As a reaction when you are attacked or subjected to an ability check or saving throw from a creature you have {@condition grappled}, {@condition devouring|lustvore|swallowing}, or {@condition swallowed|lustvore}, you gain +5 AC and stomach AC, and advantage on resisting any ability checks and saving throws from actions and ability until the end of that creatures turn.
You may use this feature a number of times equal to your Proficiency Bonus per long rest.

subclassFeature.name: Armor of Flesh
entries: At 15th level, you can use your stuffed belly to defend yourself from attacks. When you suffer damage, as a reaction you may reduce that damage by the capacity of creatures you are filled with, up to a maximum of your Fighter level + Constitution modifier. You may use this feature a number of times equal to your Proficiency Bonus per long rest.

subclassFeature.name: Inescapable
entries: At 18th level, your body becomes truly inescapable. Any creatures of your choice inside you are considered under the effects of a anti-magic field. In addition, any features that might allow them to leave your body through any method but an escape test (such as teleportation, going into the ethereal plane, etc.) instantly fails.

subclassFeature.name: Diabolical Gift
entries: At 3rd level, as a soldier for the agents of the Nine Hells, you’ve been given fiendish powers. You gain the following benefits:

items: {@b {@i Devil’s Sight:}} You can see normally in darkness, both magical and nonmagical, to a distance of 120 feet.
{@b {@i Devil’s Tongue:}} You know {@language Infernal}, the language of devils. If you already know {@language Infernal}, you learn another language of your choice.

subclassFeature.name: Hellfire Weapon
entries: At 3rd level, when you take the {@action Attack} action, you can imbue one weapon that you are holding with hellfire, transforming it into a Hellfire Weapon. It remains transformed in this way for 10 minutes or until you use this feature again, you die, or the weapon is more than 5 feet away from you for 1 minute or more. You can also end this effect early (no action required).
While transformed into a Hellfire Weapon, a weapon emits dim light in a 5 feet radius, and whenever you deal damage with the weapon, it can deal your choice of fire damage or its normal damage type.

subclassFeature.name: Infernal Wound
entries: At 3rd level, your Hellfire Weapon can inflict infernal wounds. Infernal Wound die. You have one Infernal Wound die, which is a {@dice d6}. Inflicting Infernal Wounds. Once per turn when you hit a creature with your Hellfire Weapon, you can deal extra fire damage equal to one roll of your Infernal Wound die and give the target an infernal wound.

While wounded in this way, the target takes fire damage equal to one roll of your Infernal Wound die at the start of each of its turns. This effect lasts for 1 minute, until the target regains hit points, or until the target or a creature within 5 feet of the target takes an action to stanch the wound. A target can be affected by only one instance of this feature at a time.
You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Constitution modifier (minimum of once). You regain all expended uses when you finish a short or long rest.

subclassFeature.name: Advanced Wounds
entries: At 7th level, when you roll your Infernal Wound die and roll a 6, you can apply one of the following effects:

items: {@b {@i Purulence of Minauros.}} Caustic pus erupts from the wound. Each creature in a 5 feet radius from the target takes acid damage equal to your Constitution modifier, and the target has the {@condition poisoned} condition until the start of its next turn.
{@b {@i Rupture of Cania.}} The wound ruptures with a spurt of arcane energy. The target takes force damage equal to your Constitution modifier.
{@b {@i Stygian Gangrene.}} Infernal rime spreads out from the wound. The target takes cold damage equal to your Constitution modifier, and it can’t take reactions until the start of its next turn.

subclassFeature.name: Hell-Forged Equipment
entries: At 7th level, your armor and weapons embody infernal armaments forged in the fires of Avernus, granting you the following benefits:

items: {@b {@i Fire Resistance.}} While wearing armor or wielding a shield, you have resistance to fire damage.
{@b {@i Unholy Fire.}} Damage from your weapon attacks and Fighter features ignores resistance to fire damage.

subclassFeature.name: Hellfire Surge
entries: At 10th level, when you use your Action Surge while wearing armor or wielding a shield, you can superheat your equipment, causing it to erupt with hellfire in a 10 feet radius originating from you. Each creature of your choice in the radius must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw, DC equals 8 + your Constitution modifier + Proficiency Bonus. On a failed save, a target takes fire damage equal to one roll of your Infernal Wound die and is burning. On a successful save, a target takes half as much damage and is not burning

A burning creature or object takes {@damage 1d4} fire damage at the start of each of its turns. As an action, you can extinguish fire on yourself by giving yourself the {@condition prone} condition and rolling on the ground. The fire also goes out if it is doused, submerged, or suffocated.

subclassFeature.name: Blister of Avernus
entries: At 15th level, your hellfire leaves painful, boiling blisters. When you roll a 6 on your Infernal Wound die, you can roll another {@dice d6} and add it to the damage. The maximum number of {@dice d6}s you can add to the Infernal Wound’s damage on a turn is three.

subclassFeature.name: Hellfire Condemnation
entries: At 18th level, whenever damage from your Hellfire Weapon or Infernal Wound reduces a creature to 0 hit points, the player may attempt to send its soul to the river Styx as a Lemure in a layer of the Nine Hells of your choice in {@dice 1d4} hours. If the creature isn’t revived before then, only a {@spell Wish} spell can return the creature to life. Some creatures (at DM or Player discretion as appropriate) may not be able to be sent to hell in this manner.

subclassFeature.name: Infernal Condemnation
entries: At 18th level, when you roll your Infernal Wound die, you can treat a roll of 1 as a 6.

subclassFeature.name: Ironskin
entries: Become hard as stone! Cannot be multiclassed with Bear-Totem Barbarian or Orgasmic Rager.

subclassFeature.name: Iron Skin
entries: At 3rd level, you are exceptionally tough. You reduce all non-psychic damage you take by your Proficiency Bonus. This reduction is incompatible with the damage reduction provided by Heavy Armor Master.

In addition, Whenever you take damage from an attack roll or saving throw, you may reduce the damage by your {@dice 1d10} + your Fighter level + Constitution modifier. You may use this feature a number of times equal to your Proficiency Bonus per short or long rest.
In addition, while not wearing armor, you now have an unarmored AC of 10 + your Dexterity modifier + your Constitution modifier. You may use shields with this ability.

subclassFeature.name: Dense Meal
entries: At 3rd level, you have resistance to digestion damage.

In addition, regardless of how big or small of a meal you are for your predator, you are considered to be a meal size larger than maximum capacity for the purposes of digestion speed, and for most predators take around 7 days to absorb. During which, you can live and remain in a stable condition, before you finally succumb in the final few hours. This ability supersedes all other features that affect digestion processing speed.

subclassFeature.name: Reflective Skin
entries: At 7th level, Whenever an enemy rolls a melee attack roll against you and deals damage, before you calculate resistances or reduce damage from your Iron Skin ability, you may deal an equivalent amount of damage back to the attacker of the same type, up to a maximum of your Fighter level + Constitution modifier. You may use this ability a number of times equal to your Proficiency Bonus per long rest.

subclassFeature.name: Frontline Flex
entries: At 10th level, you are able to flex your hardened muscles to resist the strongest blows. When another creature hits you with an attack or forces you to roll a Strength, Dexterity, or Constitution saving throw, you can use your reaction to add your Constitution modifier to your AC for that attack or saving throw for the ability, potentially causing the attack to miss you.

subclassFeature.name: Rock Steady
entries: At 15th level, as a bonus action, you can strengthen your stance, and gain one additional reaction until the start of your next turn

subclassFeature.name: Invulnerable
entries: At 18th level, your Iron Skin ability now reduces damage by twice your Proficiency Bonus, rather than once.

In addition, you no longer take any death saving throws. Anytime you would die or would take a death saving throw, you are instead brought to 0 hit points and are {@condition defeated|lustvore} or {@condition unconscious}.

subclassFeature.name: Vore
entries: Consumption is perhaps the oldest and most primal form of combat: As a hunter eats to survive, so too did warriors. As tribes became nations, the art of voracious combat evolved alongside them to adapt. While most soldiers and mercenaries fight with swords and bows, A soldier of vore uses these weapons alongside their natural teeth and gut to become a terribly fearsome combatant. For defeat against such predatory combatants does not simply mean being slain or captured, but rather to be gulped down into that dark abyss to await ones likely gurgling fate…

subclassFeature.name: Predatory Empowerment
entries: At 3rd level, you are empowered by your consumed enemies, and able to push through more damage to get to your next meal. When you have at least one creature inside your belly, you are considered to always roll max on your Second-Wind roll
In addition, when you swallow a creature of at least 1 capacity, you gain temporary hit points equal to its bulk + your Constitution modifier, up to a max of your total level + Constitution modifier.

subclassFeature.name: Consume the Defeated
entries: At 3rd level, you are able to use your weapons and maw to knock out your foes and more easily consume them. When you deal damage to a creature as part of a melee attack, you may attempt a {@action devour|lustvore} attack upon them without grappling them as a bonus action. If this enemy was brought to 0 hit points through this damage, you may begin a {@action devour|lustvore} contest with them with three successes as a free action instead.

subclassFeature.name: Chomp
entries: At 7th level, you can press your advantage whenever your hits strike true.
Whenever you critically hit a creature as part of a melee attack, you may choose to start a {@action devour|lustvore} contest with one success as a free action.

subclassFeature.name: Ravenous Fighter
entries: You’ve eaten so many meals you’ve lost count, and your skills show it.
At 10th level, you count as one size larger for the purpose of determining your capacity and for {@action devour|lustvore} checks.

subclassFeature.name: Surge of Hunger
entries: At 15th level, you’ve honed your body to act quickly to beat and {@action devour|lustvore} your opponent. When you use your Action Surge, you may also use your bonus action to {@action devour|lustvore} targets, and you may make {@action devour|lustvore} attacks without grappling your opponents first.

subclassFeature.name: There’s Always Another Meal
entries: At 18th level, whenever you are less than or equal to your capacity, you gain advantage on all {@action devour|lustvore} and {@action grapple} checks.

subclassFeature.name: Way of Ecstasy
entries: While many spiritual paths stray from the feelings of pleasure and ecstasy as fleeting indulgences, monks that practice the way of ecstasy revel in these feelings. Pleasure is not only enjoyable, it is required to transcend one's earthy failings and enter into a new mode of existence. Many monks that follow the Way of Ecstasy believe that to feel good is to be good, and bringing pleasure to others creates peace and prosperity.
Because of this, a monk of the Way of Ecstasy focuses around providing pleasure to themselves and to others.

subclassFeature.name: Pleasure Points
entries: At 3rd level you learn how to use your knowledge of pleasure points to make any creature squirm in pleasure. All unarmed damage and digestion damage you do may change their damage type to lewd damage. In addition, you ignore resistances to lewd damage, and immunity becomes resistance.

You also learn how to use your body more effectively against your targets when they can’t move. While a target is {@condition grappled} by you or another creature, you have advantage to hit with any unarmed strikes that deal lewd damage.

subclassFeature.name: Energize Through Pleasure
entries: At 6th level, pleasure helps to fuel your inner ki. Whenever you bring someone to 0 hit points through lewd damage, you regain 1 Ki point.
In addition, you no longer suffer {@condition exhaustion} when you orgasm or are brought to the {@condition defeated|lustvore} state through lewd damage.

subclassFeature.name: Pleasure Strike
entries: At 6th level you learn how to turn your opponents into quivering and unfocused messes. Upon hitting a target with an attack that deals lewd damage, you may spend 1 Ki points to force them to roll a Charisma saving throw. On a failure, they have disadvantage on all attack rolls and skill checks for one minute, and must roll {@status concentration} when attempting to cast any spells or keep any {@status concentration} spells ongoing vs your Ki saving throw DC. They may reroll this Charisma saving throw at the end of every turn to attempt to negate the effect early, or whenever they suffer any non-lewd damage.

subclassFeature.name: Lewd Vibrations
entries: At 11th level, as an action, you can spend 2 Ki points to send lewd vibrations through the air. All creatures of your choice within a 15 feet radius must roll a Charisma saving throw or suffer lewd damage equal to twice your martial arts die + Charisma modifier.

subclassFeature.name: Orgasmic Strike
entries: At 17th level, you become a master of the Way of Ecstasy, able to make any creature cum with a single touch. Upon hitting a target with an unarmed strike that deals lewd damage, you may spend 4 Ki points to forgo dealing damage and deliver an orgasmic strike. The target must take a Constitution saving throw. On a failure, their current hit points are reduced to 0, and are instantly {@condition defeated|lustvore} as they fall {@condition prone} and quake as they cum continuously for a number of minutes equal to your Wisdom modifier. On a success, they barely manage to prevent themselves from losing all their energy, but still orgasm and suffer {@damage 10d10} lewd damage.

subclassFeature.name: Way of the Hungry
entries: Many monk disciplines focus around honing the mind and body for a single balanced purpose: Hunger. The maker and the destroyer, all living beings feel hunger, and even the greatest emperors and kings are subject to its forceful presence. Although some can cheat their way out from its grasp, such as the undead, the rewards for mastering this primordial force is great. Acolytes of the Way of the Hungry devote their entire lives to mastering their own selves, and using their newfound wisdom to bring their own path of enlightenment to others. Sometimes forcefully.

The Way of the Hungry believes that hunger is the ultimate force in the universe. It drives all living things, and is the fuel for all life. Way of the hungry monks seek to understand this force and master the universal principles of hunger in all things. In this they often practice vorish consumption as the conjunction of hunger and conflict, and are fearsome predators in combat with a near endless appetite.

subclassFeature.name: Focus Hunger
entries: At 3rd level, you may enter a state of extreme predatory focus to rapidly consume your foes. Whenever you are able to make an unarmed attack (such as during your fury of blows), you may instead choose to take a {@action grapple} action or {@action devour|lustvore} action (if you are normally able to do a {@action devour|lustvore} action).
You also increase your capacity as if you were one size larger.

subclassFeature.name: Practiced Hunger
entries: At 6th level, you learn how to control your body to a greater degree. Whenever you make a {@action devour|lustvore} attack, you may expend a Ki point to avoid the grappling requirement for initiating a {@action devour|lustvore} check on that attack. You may use this ability any number of times during your turn.

subclassFeature.name: Unleash Hunger
entries: At 11th level, you learn the dark secrets of the path of the hungry. As an action you may spend 6 Ki points to cast {@spell inhale|lustvore}, and may continue the spell by spending 2 Ki point every turn.
You also increase your capacity as if you were one size larger.

subclassFeature.name: Master Hunger
entries: At 17th level, you are able to master your own hunger: You gain the following effects:

items: You no longer need to eat or drink, but still may do such and gain benefits for it.
Whenever you digest and process a meal, you gain temporary hit points equal to the capacity of the meal.
You can speed up your digestion to digest any meal below your maximum capacity on a short rest, and can digest your maximum capacity and above on a long rest.

Whenever you swallow a creature, you may choose to gain Ki points equal to 1/2 its bulk rounded up, up to your maximum Ki points. (a tiny or small creature would provide 1, a medium 2, and so on.). You may gain this benefit a number of times equal to your Proficiency Bonus per long rest.

subclassFeature.name: Create Thread
entries: At 3ed level you gain the ability to infuse thin threads with Ki, creating a Ki Tread. Forgoing one of your attacks as part of your attack action, you may instead spend 1 Ki point to attach two creatures, objects, or points on a surface, via a Ki Thread. If neither targets are an unwilling creature, this ability does not have a Ki cost.

These targets must be within 30 feet of you, within 30 feet of each other, and not be an object worn or carried. The Ki Tread created is exactly as long as the original distance between the two targets. If the first target is yourself, and the second target is an object weighing 10lbs. or less, you may reel the target up to 30 feet towards yourself as part of the attack action.

Ki Threads are non-magical, and near-invisible, requiring a Wisdom({@skill Perception}) check against your Ki save DC to detect. They have an AC of 10 + your Wisdom modifier, hit points equal to your Monk level, are resistant to bludgeoning, cold, and thunder damage, immune to psychic and poison damage, and can hold up to a Huge target. If your Ki Thread is made to make a saving throw, it uses your Dexterity save modifier. Creatures, objects, or points on a surface attached by Ki Treads act as if connected by rope.
You may use your Dexterity score instead of Strength on all checks relating to this effect.
A creature can, at the end of its turn, attempt to end this effect with a Strength save vs your Ki save DC.
The Ki Threads created from this feature last for 1 minute, unless they are destroyed or you dispel them earlier (no action required).

subclassFeature.name: Control Tether
entries: Starting at 6th level, you may forgo one of your attacks as part of your attack action to shorten the Ki Thread connecting two targets. When this ability is used, any creatures affected may make a Strength save vs your Ki save DC or be pulled up 30 feet towards the other tethered target.

items: If one target is two sizes larger than the other the smaller is pulled to the larger, otherwise both targets are pulled together equally.
If both targets are larger than size Huge, the DM can rule that neither target is pulled.
When a creature is pulled in this manner, you can opt to knock them {@condition prone} as part of this movement.
If they are pulled the entire length of the Ki Thread, you can choose to have them also be {@condition restrained}, which lasts until the Ki Thread is destroyed or its effect ends.

If you are the target of one of the ends of the thread and pull the wire so that you end near the other target, you can attempt a {@action devour|lustvore} check as part of that action without needing to have the target {@condition grappled}.

subclassFeature.name: Bladed Threads
entries: At 11th level, the range for Create Thread and Control Tether increases to 60 feet.
Control Tether can now retract up to 60 feet in one action.

Additionally your Ki Threads become razor-sharp hazards. When a creature passes between two targets that are tethered, you can choose to have them make a Dexterity saving throw against your Ki save DC or take slashing damage equal to 1 roll of your martial arts die and fall {@condition prone}. A creature automatically succeeds at future saves from the same Ki Thread.

subclassFeature.name: Weave Web
entries: At 17th level, infusing threads becomes second nature. Your Create Thread ability does not have a Ki cost, and you create 2 Ki Threads per attack.
In addition, your Ki Threads now last indefinitely instead of only one minute.

optionalfeature.name: Returning Weapon
entries: This magic weapon grants a +1 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with it, and it returns to wherever it was thrown or launched from immediately after it is used to make a ranged attack.

item: A simple or martial weapon with the thrown property

optionalfeature.name: Multi-Armed Form
entries: Your golem now has 4 arms, other appendages or aggressive features. When it takes an attack action it may attack one additional time.

optionalfeature.name: Grapple-Hand
entries: Your golem now can launch its hand up to 30 feet, attached by a tether line. It is able to make grapple tests up to 30 feet away, and upon a successful grapple, it may pull the {@condition grappled} creature adjacent to it as a free action. In addition, it can use its grapple hand to easily climb, and may be considered to be able to jump 30 feet up in the air or climb sheer surfaces anytime it is able to leverage its grapple hand. This infusion's range increases to 60 feet at 10th level.

optionalfeature.name: War Golem
entries: Your golem is now outfitted for war through additional armor plating and tougher flesh. It now increases its AC and stomach AC by 3 points.

optionalfeature.name: Wide Construction
entries: Your golem increases its capacity as if it was one size larger. This feature increases to two sizes larger at 10th level.

optionalfeature.name: Arcane Shield
entries: Your golem’s deflect blow ability improves, and the deflect blow ability can now impose disadvantage on any melee or ranged attack rolls from attacks it can see that target itself or another adjacent creature.

optionalfeature.name: Magical Conduit
entries: If you can see your golem and are within 30 feet, you may use your bonus action to allow it to cast a cantrip from your list of known cantrips as its action. If you can see your golem and are within 30 feet, you may cast self spells on your golem without having to touch them.

optionalfeature.name: Golem of Holding
entries: Your golem is considered to have the {@feat Stomach of Holding|lustvore} feat.

optionalfeature.name: Symbiotic Golem
entries: While a creature is inside the golem, the creature no longer needs to eat or drink. In addition, when a golem takes a long rest with at least 1 capacity worth of creatures inside of it, the golem restores its full hit points and gains temporary hit points equal to your Artificer Level + Intelligence modifier at the end of the long rest.

optionalfeature.name: Arcane Blaster
entries: Your battle golem may now use its Force Empowered Strike ability as a ranged attack with a range of 60 feet. This improves at 10th level to 120 feet.

optionalfeature.name: Orgasmic Battery
entries: While a creature is inside of it, your golem can stimulate it in order to power itself through the creature's sexual energy. As an action, it may deal {@dice 2d6} + your Intelligence modifier lewd damage to one creature inside of it. The golem gains temporary hit points equal to the damage dealt, not counting any damage done past 0 hit points. This infusion improves to {@dice 4d6} + your Intelligence modifier lewd damage at 10th level.

optionalfeature.name: Voracious Protocol
entries: Your golem may {@action Devour|lustvore} as a bonus action upon successfully grappling a creature during its turn.

optionalfeature.name: Gulping Golem
entries: Your golem counts as one size larger for purposes of grappling and devour contest checks when they are the grappler/predator.

optionalfeature.name: Uncanny Appearance
entries: Your golem is now indistinguishable in appearance from a human, or another race of your choosing. Due to their more realistic appearance, they gain proficiency in {@skill Persuasion}.

optionalfeature.name: Maid Modifications
entries: Your golem now takes on the appearance of a maid. It gains the {@spell prestidigitation} and {@spell mending} cantrip, the {@feat Healer} feat, and is considered to always have a {@item healer's kit} that replenishes all charges on a long rest. The golems restores the max amount of hit points possible on any healing roll when the target is inside them (excluding themselves).

optionalfeature.name: Lewd Appendages
entries: Your golem is now equipped with various lewd devices, appendages, and upgrades. It may deal lewd damage in place of any damage, including its digestion damage. In addition, when your golem grapples a creature, it gains advantage on all attacks that do lewd damage against that {@condition grappled} creature.

optionalfeature.name: Alchemical Repurposing
entries: Upon digesting meal equal to its capacity, instead of gaining temporary hit points, your golem may reuse its nutrients to create a number of potions equal to its Constitution modifier within itself. These potions may either be a {@item potion of healing}, {@item potion of poison}, or a {@item philter of love}, in any combination. These potions can be regurgitated out through any orifice or piping as an action and fed to an adjacent creature or container. It can hold a number of potions equal to its Constitution modifier. This infusion improves at 10th level to being able to hold and create twice its Constitution modifier worth of potions.

optionalfeature.name: Recycling Module
entries: Your golem’s digestion ignores digestion resistances, and immunities become resistances. In addition, it can now digest anything except magical items. This includes inanimate material such as stone, metal, diamonds, etc. These materials now count as food for the purposes of various golem effects. In addition, upon digesting a meal of inorganic materials, It can choose to forgo the normal digestion bonuses (such as healing and temporary hit points) to create new objects that are smaller than the meal, and is capable of transmuting materials into other materials. However these objects are always somewhat crude, and do not pass up to close inspection or very fine tasks (ex. stamped gold coins look crude and “off”, precise lockpicking tools are a bit too blocky, etc.)

optionalfeature.name: Override Link
entries: Your golem is now designed to safely store you, and allow you to link into its body to become an extension of yourself. Upon gaining the {@condition swallowed|lustvore} condition inside your golem, you can integrate into your golem as a free action. While integrated into the golem, you are considered to be the golem, and see and feel what it feels and able to use its abilities during your turn. The golem can still feel what is going on and can mentally communicate with you. The golem no longer has its own actions or count in the initiative while you are integrated inside it. Due to your golem assisting you, you gain the following ability while integrating with your golem:

entries.name: Stronger Together.
entries: You may now use your bonus action to {@action Dash}, {@action Disengage}, {@action Use an Object}, or {@action Attack} (one weapon attack only). You also gain one additional reaction.

While integrated, you now make all your physical tests with the golems stats, and you now use the golems attacks in place of your own. However you can also use your spells while controlling the golem as if you were the golem, as well as any other abilities you might have. Attacks that target the golem can force you to take {@status concentration} checks, which you do with advantage.

optionalfeature.name: Large
entries: Your golem is now Large, and gains all the appropriate benefits for the size increase. This adds an additional {@dice 1d8} to the damage of their Force Empowered Strike. However, you now must spend 1 spell slot of every spell level that you know in order to reactivate it, rather than simply a 1st-level spell slot. (ex. At 9th level, you would need to expend a 1st, 2nd, and 3rd-level spell slot when you took your minute to revive the golem.). In addition, your golems hit points are calculated as your Intelligence modifier + golem's Constitution modifier + 10 times your Artificer Level

optionalfeature.name: Magic Reservoir
entries: A golem has a pool of magic equal to your Intelligence modifier + Proficiency Bonus. As the golems action, it can cast any spell you have prepared by expending a number of its magic pool points equal to the spell's level. It can replenish its magic reservoir by digesting a meal equal to its capacity or greater instead of gaining temporary hit points.

optionalfeature.name: Create Minor Golem
entries: By spending a long rest and 1000gp and one of your infusions, you are able to create a {@creature lesser golem|lustvore}. This golem does not count against the maximum number of golems you can have. This golem comes with a single golem infusion of your choice that you know, and this added infusion on the lesser golem does not count against the number of infusions you can have active at one time. This infusion may never be changed. It may not have any of the greater golem infusions you gain access to at 9th level.

If this golem is ever reduced to 0 hit points, it is destroyed and cannot be revived like a normal golem. However, you always have a copy of its core, and can recreate it with another ritual after a long rest, spending the same gold cost.
The golem follows all other rules of normal golems.

optionalfeature.name: Predator
entries: You gain additional +2 to your {@skill Athletics} modifier.

optionalfeature.name: Aftershocks
entries: When you hit a creature with a weapon attack or unarmed strike, you can expend one superiority die to cause orgasmic aftershocks. The target must make a Constitution saving throw, on a failed save the target is overcome with pleasure. Until the end of your next turn, their movement speed is halved, and if they take an action that affects a foe (attacks, spells, AoEs, etc.) they take lewd damage equal to 2 rolls of the superiority die from orgasmic aftershocks.

optionalfeature.name: Choke
entries: When you make a {@action Devour|lustvore} check as prey to resist being devoured, you can expend one superiority die and add the die to the roll, provided you aren't {@condition incapacitated}.

optionalfeature.name: Entice
entries: When you hit a creature with a weapon attack or unarmed strike, you can expend one superiority die to entice it's appetite towards you. You add one superiority die to the attack's damage roll, and the target must make a Wisdom saving throw. On a failed save the target is compelled to {@action devour|lustvore} you. All rolls and actions that don't involve {@condition devouring|lustvore} you are made with disadvantage and the creature can bypass the need of grapple to start {@action devour|lustvore} against you until the end of your next turn.

optionalfeature.name: Gulp
entries: When you make a {@action Devour|lustvore} check as predator to swallow another creature, you can expend one superiority die and add the die to the roll, provided you aren't {@condition incapacitated}.

optionalfeature.name: Tease
entries: When you hit a creature with a weapon attack or unarmed strike, you can expend one superiority die to attempt to charm the target. You add the superiority die to the attack's damage roll. The target must make a Charisma saving throw or become {@condition charmed} to you until the end of your next turn.
