Regardless of whether the creature succeeds or fails this save, when you use this maneuver you can deal lewd damage instead of the attack’s normal damage type when you use this maneuver.

feat.name: Undeath
entries: Taking this feat gives a number of changes:

items: You count as undead for purposes of effects other than healing spells.
You do not need to breath, eat, or drink.
You can gain the effects of 8 hours of sleep in 4 hours, but during which you are still unaware of your surroundings.

items.name: Undead Fortitude
entries: If damage reduces you to 0 hit points, you must make a Constitution saving throw with a DC of 5 + the damage taken, unless the damage is radiant or from a critical hit. On a success, you drop to 1 hit point instead. After the saving throw succeeds, you can't use this feature again until you finish a long rest.

items: Upon taking this feat, you get a {@filter CR1 summoned monster companion|bestiary|Challenge Rating=[&1]}, to use as a mount or a friend. Whether you choose a base CR1 enemy, or you decide to create your own CR1 creature, you must put them into the Item Crafting channel and ping the crafting helper role so that your companion can be approved. Please include a link to your character's sheet when you make this post.
This creature counts as a class summon, so you may give it vore feats and use your own vore stats for it as with any other class summon.
If the creature dies, you may resummon them at the end of a long rest.

feat.name: Arcane Siphon
entries: Your stomach is protected with powerful and mysterious wards that imprisons your prey and siphons off their magical energy. You gain the following benefits:

items: Once you finish digesting and processing a spellcaster, that spellcaster's list of prepared or known spells is available to you. You lose access to that list after 24 hours. You may only cast a spell from the list if you have a spell slot of the appropriate level.

As an action, you can siphon off the magical energy from your prey. You deal your digestion damage in psychic damage to a creature inside you, and can immediately cast a spell you have prepared or know that takes an action or bonus action as part of this action. This feature may be used once per long rest.

feat.name: Anti-Magic Prison
entries: Your stomach is the doom of all mages, as they quickly find themselves unable to rely on their spells as your stomach gurgles around them and drains their power. You gain the following benefits:

items: Creatures and objects inside your stomach can't be detected by magical means, such as {@spell scrying} or {@spell locate person}. Spells that attempt to do so fail.
All {@status concentration} checks are made with disadvantage inside your gut.
You gain resistance to all damage done from spells and other magical effects done from inside you.
You have advantage on all saving throws against spell effects from spells cast inside your belly.
Teleportation spells targeting creatures within your belly no longer have any effect, and always fail. A creature within your belly cannot escape your body through any means of teleportation.

feat.name: Ambush Predator
entries: You have mastered the art of the surprise attack and use it to gulp down unwary foes. You gain the following benefits:

items: You may attempt to {@action Devour|LustVore} a creature without grappling them first if you are Hidden from them. If successful, you gain one additional success on this devour and the prey is considered muffled for the duration of the devour contest. While muffled they can not convey intelligible words (for use in spells or other means) and creatures have disadvantage on {@skill Perception} checks to hear them.

You have learned how to keep your prey quieter while {@condition devouring|lustvore} them. Whenever you are a predator in a devour contest with one or more successes, you may take a bonus action to muffle your prey. While muffled they can not convey intelligible words (for use in spells or other means) and creatures have disadvantage on {@skill Perception} checks to hear them.

feat.name: Aerial Predator
entries: You're able to use gravity to its full effect to gulp down prey through one orifice or another. You gain the following effects:

items: When falling down above a creature's head or body, as an attack you can attempt to land upon an enemy below and roll a devour test without grappling them first. If you are falling down from 40 feet or greater, you gain an additional success on a successful devour check. If you are falling down from 80 feet or greater, you gain two additional successes. On a failure, you fall on the ground {@condition prone} and adjacent to the enemy, expend all remaining movement you have, and take falling damage equal to {@dice 1d6} for every 10 feet you fell, to a maximum of {@dice 20d6} and a minimum of {@dice 1d6} damage

When an enemy falls from above you and will land on or adjacent to you, you can attempt a devour check as a reaction without grappling them first. Upon success, you gain one additional success in the devour contest. If two aerial predators are attempting to use this feat on one another (one from below, one from above), the one on the ground/below will get the first attempt.

feat.name: Assimilation
entries: Characters with this feat can steal the abilities of those they eat. When you finish digesting a creature, you may choose one of the features it possessed and adapt it into your own body. These abilities scale to your size and level at DM's discretion. You may only have one assimilated bonus at one time. You may acquire one of the following:

items: A movement speed (fly, swim, or climb) that cannot surpass your current base movement speed.
An increase of up to additional 10 feet of walking speed as long as that speed is faster than yours by at least that much.
A natural attack.
Its natural unarmored AC, up to a maximum boost of your proficeny modifier. (i.e. at most 10 + your Dexterity modifier + your Proficency Bonus)
A special sense: {@sense Darkvision}, {@sense blindsight} (up to 10 feet), excluding {@sense truesight}.
One damage resistance.
Temporary hit points equal to the creature's CR.

entries: Should you ever be killed and then revived, you lose your assimilated bonus upon resurrection or reformation.
{@i Note: If you have the {@feat soul absorption|lustvore} feat, it should generally be allowed to absorb and assimilate a creature at the same time.}

feat.name: Belly Shield
entries: You are most comfortable when sporting a massive belly, and are able to use your own mass to ward off attacks. When you are filled with greater than your base bulk's worth, you are considered to be in half cover against all attacks.

feat.name: Belly Pet
entries: There is no place like home, and no home as comfortable as a cozy squeezing belly. So much so that you can form a supernatural connection with your “home”. You gain the following abilities:

items: While inside a creature who is {@condition willing|lustvore} to make the connection, you can spend 1 hour making a connection with your predator, massaging and doing other rituals to solidify your bond with your predator. At the end of an hour, this creates a {@i Belly Home}. Upon being digested by your predator that you have a belly home connection with, your soul moves to reside in your predators guts, and the predator can interact with you as if they had the {@feat soul absorption|lustvore} feat: This means they can mentally speak with you, and the predator of your belly home can choose to reform you after consuming a meal of similar size to you and taking a long rest. This belly home lasts until you spend a long rest outside of it. You may only have one belly home at a time, and creating a second belly home replaces the first.
While inside your belly home, you no longer need to eat or drink. In addition, you regain all your hit dice on a long rest rather than half.
Once per long rest, you can teleport into your belly home as if the predator casted {@spell bellyport ally|LustVore} on you at DC of 15 or your spell save DC, whichever is higher.

As an action, the user can pick a creature within 5 feet that has someone inside them and massage at their victim's outline to either enhance or neutralize digestion. All prey inside their belly gain resistance or vulnerability to all digestion damage until the start of the helper's next turn, declared by the belly rubber. (This can be used on yourself, another creature, or someone that you are inside of.)

Whenever you could take the struggle action, you can instead choose to Massage. You provide the predator with advantage on a single attack, grapple or devour test, or saving throw until the end of their next turn.
Your massaging skills are quite excellent and give you advantage on {@skill Persuasion}, {@skill Deception}, {@skill Insight}, and other social checks while you are able to leverage your skills.

feat.name: Belly Mage
entries: A massaging or churning belly does little to distract you from your magical focus. You gain the following abilities:

items: While inside a belly, you gain advantage on all {@status concentration} checks, and you do not need to make {@status concentration} checks to cast a spell if you have not suffered damage since the end of your last turn.
While inside a belly, you do not have disadvantage on spell attacks vs your predator.
While inside a belly, you add your proficiency modifier to all spell damage, and to all healing spells.

feat.name: Belly Fighter
entries: No longer do the squishing walls of a belly compress you into a feeble state. You have learned how to position yourself and press back against the walls enough to give you space to fight back! Or at least, to struggle and do your actions without as much resistance!

While you are inside another creature, you are no longer {@condition restrained}. Instead, all attacks against you gain advantage, and your speed is 0 as you are still trapped within a belly, even if you are able to move around a bit more freely!

feat.name: Bloodhound
entries: Your sense of smell is superb, able to track down any prey that thinks they can hide from you. You gain the following effects:

items: You are proficient in {@skill Survival} skill. If you were already proficient, you gain expertise in {@skill Survival} skill.

You can spend a bonus action on an adjacent creature or an item bearing their scent or other unique distinguishable trait. Doing so marks the creature for 24 hours. While you have marked a creature, you have advantage on all ability checks to track them. If you use this ability again, you replace the old scent with the new one.

You can detect {@condition invisible} or concealed creatures whom you have marked through this feat within 60 feet, and do not suffer disadvantage on attack rolls against said creatures because of concealment or invisibility.

feat.name: Bond Beyond Death
entries: You and your companion are so close that you can rescue each other even from the abyss. This feat has the following effects:

items: If both you and a trusted ally have this feat, whenever one ally gets digested or their body is otherwise completely destroyed, the other can reform them inside their own body. This process requires one long rest, and requires consuming a meal of the same size class or larger than the person to be reformed.
This can be done so long as they were digested or otherwise died in the last month.

feat.name: Chaotic Imbuement
entries: You are imbued with chaotic energies which can be channeled for powerful, if concerningly unpredictable, effects.

Once per short or long rest, after hitting a creature with a ranged, melee, or spell attack roll, you can imbue the strike with chaotic magic. For that strike, you may gain an additional {@dice 1d12} damage, and roll a {@dice 1d100} on the {@table chaos magic table|lustvore} after you deal damage. You may then choose to apply the effect to yourself, or to your target.

feat.name: Choking Hazard
entries: Your short nature but wide assets make predators underestimate just how difficult it would be to devour you, some swallow too swiftly without realizing the consequences of their actions.

items: Your Bulk increases one stage.

Any time you successfully make an escape attempt or your predator fails a devour check on you, you can deal {@dice 1d4} bludgeoning damage as they choke on your assets. At 5th level it becomes {@dice 2d4}, at 11th level it becomes {@dice 3d4} and at 17th level it becomes {@dice 4d4}.
Something about you makes preds want to put you in their mouth, and will more often approach you as a potential meal, or potential belly pet.

feat.name: Comfort in Digestion
entries: Due to your body, or experiences, you have learned how to take pleasure in digestion and last longer in a churning belly!

items: When you suffer digestion damage, you can use your reaction to feel empowered, and gain {@dice 1d4} to any roll until the end of your next turn.
You have resistance to non-magical digestion damage.

feat.name: Compress Belly
entries: You are able to compress your prey in a way that hides their outline to all but the most keen observers, and even muffles sounds. You gain the following abilities:

items: Creatures and objects inside your belly count as one size smaller while inside you for the purposes of how much capacity they take up.
Your belly suppresses sounds, making it impossible for those who are not adjacent or have their ear up to your belly to hear. Unless you desire otherwise.
When your belly is small enough, people often will not suspect you have eaten someone, and depending on capacity may not even give your belly a second glance.

While equal to or under ½ capacity, your belly looks more pregnant, fat, or otherwise bulky. It may draw some attention, but most common folk will not instantly assume you've eaten someone. If they do have a reason to suspect or otherwise notice something strange, they will require a DC 15 {@skill Perception} check to confirm their suspicions.
Above ½ capacity, this feat no longer works to effectively hide prey, although your belly is still smaller than expected!

feat.name: Deliciously Delectable
entries: Your curves are divine, your scent delectable, and your taste is pure ecstasy. One seductive glance or slight lick is all it takes to send predators (and even non-predators!) wild. You gain the following effects:

items: You're adept at convincing predators to eat you, and gain advantage on all {@skill Persuasion} and {@skill Performance} tests that involve leveraging yourself into a meal/belly pet/etc. for a predator.
While grappling or {@condition devouring|lustvore} you, or being {@condition grappled} or devoured by you, a creature suffers disadvantage on all checks that don't involve you.
A predator needs one more success than normal to successfully swallow you as they savor your taste and feel.
Predators will sense your delicious nature, and will more often approach you as a potential meal, or potential belly pet.

feat.name: Digestive Ecstasy
entries: Your stomach is not merely pleasurable, it's orgasmic heaven. Every touch of digestive juices is enough to change the tune of even the most fearful, stoic, and resistant prey. Melting away has never felt so good. You gain the following effects:

items: Your digestive juices are incredibly pleasurable and distracting. As a bonus action, you can make your digestive juices intoxicating. All prey inside your belly make a Wisdom saving throw vs 8 + your Charisma modifier + Proficiency Bonus or your spell save DC, whichever is higher. On a failure, they are {@condition stunned} until the start of your next turn as they are overwhelmed with pleasure, and unable to take actions. Failure of three of these saves in a row means they succumb to the pleasure, and are considered {@condition incapacitated} until digestion stops or they are digested.
Creatures inside you roll at disadvantage when trying to break free from the {@condition charmed} condition or other charm-like effects.
Your stomach now deals lewd digestion damage. You may suppress this to deal normal acid/bludgeoning damage instead.

feat.name: Elemental Belly
entries: Your belly has strange, elemental properties that aid it in suppressing and digesting your meals.

When you take this lewd feat, pick a damage type between lightning, fire, cold, and poison. You roll an additional {@dice 1d6} digestion damage, and may make your digestion damage count as your respective chosen element.

feat.name: Egg Entrapment
entries: Your body is able to entrap your prey into eggs, making them easier to manage. You gain the following effects:

items: When a creature within you is either {@condition willing|lustvore}, {@condition defeated|lustvore}, or if a creature otherwise does not resist, you can decide to begin packing them into an egg somewhere within your body, or begin forming an egg around them and trap them within instead of digesting and processing them. Upon finishing a short or long rest, the target is fully enclosed inside an egg. They are considered {@condition blinded} and {@condition restrained}. They do not require food or water while inside an egg inside a predator, and do not require food or water for a year while outside a predator. They also are considered one size smaller for purposes of capacity due to their tight compression in an egg. This does not provide the creature within an egg any immunity to rubs, spells, or other affects that may normally target prey within a belly or full cover, and the prey within may still benefit from any feats or features that require being within a predator so long as their egg is contained within a creature.
A creature with an egg inside them can choose to release a target out of an egg over the course of one minute as their body acids gently dissolve the egg without harming the individual inside.
While outside a creature, an egg can be smashed open with an DC 15 {@skill Athletics} check.

While outside of a creature and outside of combat, a conscious creature in an egg can attempt to break free once every hour with an {@skill Athletics} check with a DC equal to 10 + your Constitution modifier. While in combat and outside of a creature, a conscious creature in an egg may at the end of their turn use an action to attempt to break free with an {@skill Athletics} check of the same DC.
These eggs are considered objects for purposes of spells and effects, until broken.
A creature with only a number of eggs inside them equal to ½ or less of their capacity can pass off as pregnant without difficulty.
You gain one additional vore or lewd feat upon taking this feat.

feat.name: Escape Artist
entries: Thanks to your size, you're often targeted by hungry predators. As such, you've developed a number of counter techniques to thwart those who want you as a bite-sized snack. You gain the following benefits:

items: If a predator would successfully completely swallow you as part of a devour contest, you may use your reaction to roll an escape attempt following escape rules for a devour contest. On a success, the enemy does not count a success.
When you have the {@condition swallowed|lustvore} condition, you do not have disadvantage on your ability checks.

feat.name: Energy Drain
entries: You can sap the energy from your prey rather than digesting them down for nutrients. You gain the following ability:

items: Anytime you are digesting a prey, you can declare to energy drain them instead. Your digestion damage becomes psychic damage, and this is considered magical damage for the purposes of overcoming resistances. Creatures {@condition incapacitated} and digested through energy drain follow the same rules as normal digestion. However, the prey is no longer considered expired, and instead remains {@condition defeated|lustvore} during this time. Once fully processed, the prey gains one level of {@condition exhaustion}, and cannot be energy drained again for another 24 hours.
When you use this feature to digest and process, you gain all the normal benefits from digestion, including special features that rely on digestion.

As an action, your gut can sap the energy from your prey. All creatures of your choice in you must roll a Wisdom saving throw vs 8 + your Charisma modifier + Proficiency Bonus or your spell save DC, whichever is higher. On a failure, they take 3 levels of {@condition exhaustion}, up to a maximum of 5 total levels of {@condition exhaustion}. You cannot use this feature again until you finish a short or long rest.

feat.name: Empowering Prey
entries: Your presence in a predator's belly is enough to turn the meekest of predators into confident dominators. And you are particularly nutritious… You gain the following effects:

items: While inside a creature, you may extend feelings of pleasure and confidence as a bonus action. They gain an advantage to all skill checks, saving throws, and attacks until the end of your next turn. You may do this once per short rest.

Your predator finds themselves more comfortable in social situations with your reassuring and pleasurable presence inside. They gain advantage on {@skill Performance}, {@skill Persuasion}, {@skill Intimidation}, and {@skill Deception} checks.
Upon being digested, your predator gains an amount of temporary hit points equal to your level + your Charisma modifier.
Due to your approachable presence, predators will more often approach you as a potential meal, or potential belly pet.

feat.name: Experienced Predator
entries: You have consumed countless meals, {@condition willing|lustvore} or otherwise, and have learned how to more effectively devour your prey. You gain the following effects:

items: You become proficient in either {@skill Athletics} or {@skill Acrobatics}, and if you do not already have expertise for your chosen skill, you gain expertise for it.
Once per short rest, you may give yourself advantage in a devour check as a predator.

feat.name: Experienced Prey
entries: You have been eaten, or at least a target for predators, more times than you can count. This experience has given you insight into how to avoid being eaten, or at least control who eats you. You gain the following abilities:

items: You become proficient in either {@skill Athletics} or {@skill Acrobatics}, and if you do not already have expertise for your chosen skill, you gain expertise for it.
Whenever you have the {@condition willing|lustvore} condition, you can choose to give any predator {@condition devouring|lustvore} you two extra successes.
Once per short rest, you may give yourself advantage in a devour contest as prey.

feat.name: Eyes of the Pred
entries: Your uniquely empathetic nature lets you cross the pred/prey divide and gain an even closer bond with your predator. While you have the {@condition swallowed|lustvore} condition, and if your predator is {@condition willing|lustvore}, as a free action you are able to establish a bond with them to see out of their eyes and feel their senses, allowing you to do the following abilities:

items: You are able to cast spells as if you were standing in the predator's square without the {@condition swallowed|lustvore} condition, as you channel the magic through their eyes and body.
You and your predators spoken words become unnaturally clear to one another, and you are always able to hear each other.
You are able to project your voice out from the pred as if you were speaking from the preds mouth.
You no longer need to make {@status concentration} checks when casting spells inside of them, so long as you have not suffered digestion damage since the end of your last turn.

When you make a {@status concentration} check while you are inside a friendly or otherwise allied predator, you gain your predator's Constitution modifier as a bonus to your {@status concentration} saving throw.

feat.name: Familiar Bonding
entries: When you are bonded to someone as a belly pet, you gain additional benefits listed below:

items: You can communicate with your bonded partner telepathically. They are able to respond to this telepathy as if they had your telepathy feature at unlimited range.

As an action or bonus action, your bonded partner can look out from your senses, and can hear and see what you see. However during this time they are considered {@condition blinded}, as they can only see out from your senses. They can end this effect as a bonus action or action.
When your bonded partner casts a spell, they can cast it from your location. You must spend your reaction to cast the spell.

If your partner is a spellcaster, you can cast any cantrips they possess. If you are not a spellcaster your spellcasting stat is either Intelligence, Wisdom or Charisma and you have a spell save DC of 8 + Proficiency Bonus + your chosen Spellcasting Attribute modifier (chosen at bonding).

If you are within 100 feet, as an action, your bonded partner can summon you to their side. You are instantly teleported to a spot within 30 feet of them, or inside their belly. If you are inside another creature, the creature must make a Charisma saving throw against your partner's spell save DC. If they don't have a spell save DC, it is 8 + Proficiency Bonus + either your Intelligence, Wisdom or Charisma modifier (Chosen at bonding). You use whichever is higher. On fail, you are teleported. You can use this ability once per short rest.
Should you ever die, your bonded partner can revive and summon you through a 1 hour ritual on a short or long rest. They can only do this once per long rest.

feat.name: Feeder
entries: You not only adventure with predators, but you also actively encourage their gluttonous habits. You gain the following effects:

items: Whenever you make a {@action Shove} action, you can push a target creature into a creature that isn't yourself. The potential predator automatically starts a {@condition devouring|lustvore} contest with one success against the shoved creature. If it was already in a devour contest, it adds one success to the devour contest. Either of these can only happen if you have succeeded in the contested shove check.

When you take the shove action to shove a creature into another creature to begin or continue a devour contest, you may opt to use your {@skill Acrobatics} in place of {@skill Athletics} for that shove action, and you may ignore normal size restrictions on the shove action for this shove. Otherwise, you must use {@skill Athletics} for the shove action, and you are limited by the usual limitations of the shove action.

You may try to force-feed yourself to another creature. As an attack, you may start a devour contest against a creature or continue a devour contest with a creature, with you as the prey and without needing to grapple them first. If you win this devour contest, the creature gains one success towards {@condition devouring|lustvore} you.

You're adept at finding deals for food for your companions. Bulk orders for rations, food, and other sustenance cost half as much, and you have an eye for picking out possible prey. You gain advantage on {@skill Perception} and {@skill Investigation} tests for purposes of finding suitable prey, and advantage on {@skill Insight} tests to determine if other creatures may be voraphiles or {@condition willing|lustvore} prey…

feat.name: Friendly Consumption
entries: You have learned how to more quickly consume your friends to protect them. You gain the following abilities:

items: When {@condition devouring|lustvore} a friendly, allied, or {@condition willing|lustvore} creature, you gain 2 additional successes on your devour contest, and you never need to grapple them first in order to initiate a devour contest.

When a friendly, allied or {@condition willing|lustvore }creature adjacent to you or within unarmed reach is the target of a grapple or devour action, you may use your reaction to attempt to devour them first. Make an opposed devour test against the attacking creature. On a success you start a devour contest with the friendly, allied, or {@condition willing|lustvore} creature instead, gaining the appropriate 2 additional successes.

feat.name: Gluttonous Gullet
entries: Your desire to gobble up your prey as fast as possible has caused your body to more easily suck and pull down all potential meals into your waiting guts.
Before you make a devour contest check where you are the predator, you may choose to gain a {@hit –5} penalty to your roll. On a successful check, you gain two successes rather than one.

feat.name: Greedy Predator
entries: What you eat is yours, and yours alone! It'd take an army to get you to spit up a good meal.

You have advantage on saves against effects that would make you spit up your prey, and can give yourself advantage to keep prey down as a reaction up to a number of times equal to your proficiency modifier per long rest, but you are unable to willingly regurgitate prey.

feat.name: Gut Crush
entries: Your muscles and flesh crush your prey into submission. You gain the following abilities:

items: You gain a new natural weapon attack that you are considered proficient in, “Gutcrush”. When a creature is inside of you, you can make this melee attack in place of one of your attacks to attack that creature. This attack deals {@dice 2d6} + Strength modifier bludgeoning damage on a hit. If a predator has extra attacks, this attack may be used in place of any number of their attacks.
Your hardened muscles and thick skin give you +2 to your stomach AC.
When you deal digestion damage, you can choose to deal bludgeoning damage instead of acid damage.

feat.name: Gut Punch
entries: Your knowledge of how to hit someone where it's most sensitive. Whether through strength, cunning, or pleasure, you know how to hit just the right spot, which gives you an edge when it comes to striking.

items: You gain a new natural melee weapon you are proficient in that deals {@dice 1d6} + Dexterity modifier damage. When you attack, you may choose if this damage is piercing, bludgeoning, slashing, or lewd damage.
Upon damaging an enemy with any melee attack, you may attempt an escape check as a bonus action if you are devoured.

feat.name: Gut Slut
entries: You can't get enough of being inside a belly. You dream of being squeezed by fleshy walls and dominated by a predator. You can't help but squirm a little more towards your fate… And often, you're such a pleasurable meal that even the most ravenous predator will consider sparing you… If only to enjoy you once more. You gain the following effects:

items: A predator needs one less success than normal for your size to swallow you.

While inside another intelligent creature, as an action you can wriggle, squirm, and massage in a pleasurable manner. The predator must take a Charisma saving throw vs 8 + your {@skill Persuasion} or {@skill Performance} modifier.  On a failure, they consider you pleasing enough to save temporarily, and cannot attempt to digest you for 24 hours so long as you do not take any hostile actions against them, such as dealing damage, violently struggling, etc. The predator does not have to let you go, and in fact may often attempt to keep inside for further pleasure. You may use this feature once per predator per long rest.
Predators will sense your gut-slut nature, and more often approach you as a potential meal, or potential belly pet.

feat.name: Grasping Hands
entries: You only need one sturdy hand to subdue and smother your prey, leaving your other hand free to grab another. You gain the following effects:

items: Whenever you take the {@action grapple} action, you can immediately {@action grapple} an additional target within 5 feet as a bonus action if a target is available.

Whenever you cast a cantrip, make a contested check, or make an attack that targets one {@condition grappled} target, you can do the same to one other target you have {@condition grappled} as a bonus action.

Whenever you take the devour action to start a new devour contest or continue an ongoing one, you may attempt to start a new devour contest or continue an ongoing one with one additional {@condition grappled} or {@condition devouring|lustvore} target within 5 feet as a bonus action.
Whenever you are able to make an attack of opportunity, you can attempt a {@action grapple} instead.
When you take this feat, you may choose one (or more) trigger that will cause the {@condition Lewded|lustvore} condition on your character.
You gain one additional vore feat upon taking this feat.

feat.name: Huge
entries: Increases your size to Huge permanently, lowers your AC by 2, and you have disadvantage to all Dexterity checks and saving throws.

Your increased size makes daily life difficult. Your size (and often appetite) draws unwanted attention, and many will regard you with suspicion and restained hostility. In addition, most civilizations do not have accommodations for your size, and it is difficult to find weapons, armor, and gear for your size, and you have disadvantage on using equipment not meant for your tremendous size.

feat.name: Hyper
entries: You are beyond curvaceous, and you have learned how to use your expansive features to their full potential. You gain the following effects:

items: Your natural assets are now considered a melee weapon that you are proficient in and use your charisma to hit, and deal {@dice 1d8} + Charisma modifier damage.
Whenever you land a critical hit against an adjacent creature with an attack that deals lewd damage, you may roll one additional damage die.
Once per turn, when you hit an adjacent creature with an attack that deals lewd damage, you may take a bonus action to push it 5 feet in a direction of your choosing or automatically grapple them.

feat.name: Hypnotic Hunter
entries: You're a master of coaxing creatures into giving themselves up to you, weaving magic and seductive behavior into an irresistible combination. You gain the following benefits:

items: Creatures charmed by you do not consider {@condition devouring|lustvore} and grappling as hostile actions for the purposes of ending a charm effect early. However, dealing damage still does, and depending on circumstances they still may not want to be eaten even if they don't regard it as hostile and may choose to resist.

When a creature is {@condition charmed} by you, you may use your bonus action to force them to make a Wisdom saving throw at DC 8 + your Charisma modifier + Proficiency Bonus, or your spell save DC, whichever is higher. On a failure, they gain the {@condition willing|lustvore} condition so long as the charm continues.
A creature who is {@condition willing|lustvore} towards you is {@condition incapacitated} while they are in your belly and are still {@condition charmed} and {@condition willing|lustvore}.

feat.name: Indomitable Acid
entries: Your digestive fluids affect a far wider range of materials than normal, and are much stronger. You gain the following effects:

items: Your body now digests wood, stone, metal and other such non organic substances, and can even gain sustenance from it. In general, you need 5x times more mass of non-organic items to get the same amount of food as normal meals. However you cannot digest magical items.
Creatures that would otherwise be immune to your digestion damage are considered resistant, and creatures that would otherwise be considered resistant take full damage.
You add your proficiency modifier in additional digestion damage.

feat.name: Insatiable Hunger
entries: Your hunger never seems satiated. You must be fed, always. You gain the following effects:

items: You count as one size larger for the purpose of determining your Capacity.
Once per turn after you swallow a creature or critically hit on a devour attack, you may move up to 5 feet and make a devour check against a creature without grappling them first.

feat.name: Internal Spell
entries: You can direct your spells into your belly. This gives you the following effects:

items: Whenever you cast a spell that can target creatures other than yourself, you may instead choose to cast it inside your belly as if you had line of sight or touch. If the spell has an area of effect, that area becomes all targets within your belly. If the spell requires specific targets, you may choose any valid within. You are never affected by your own spells cast internally.
Any spells cast within you gain an increase to damage or healing equal to your proficiency bonus.

feat.name: Large
entries: Perhaps due to your appetite, or due to other circumstances, you have become larger than most others of your race. You gain the following effects:

items: You permanently increase your size by one step and gain all the appropriate benefits for a permanent size increase (Such as increased bulk, for devour contests, space you take up, etc.)
All goods and services are now 2x more expensive to cater to your increased size. You must buy 2x more rations, rooms cost 2x more, weapons and armor for your size are 2x more.
Your increased size may cause other problems and unwanted attention.

prerequisite.other: Medium or smaller size, Incompatible with Small feat.

feat.name: Level Headed
entries: Having been on the receiving- and giving- ends of lewds many times before, you are not as easily flustered as a novice.

As a reaction on taking lewd damage, you may give yourself resistance to lewd damage that lasts till the start of your next turn, up to a number of times equal to your proficiency modifier per long rest.

feat.name: Long Tongue
entries: For one reason or another, your tongue is exceptionally long, dexterous, and strong, or you have another way to pull prey into your mouth from range. You gain the following abilities:

items: When you take the {@action grapple} or {@action devour|lustvore} actions, you may make the test from up to 15 feet away rather than adjacent. On a success, the target is pulled adjacent.
You now gain a new attack, tongue lash. This tongue strike has a range of 15/30 feet, is considered a ranged attack, and deals {@dice 1d8} + Dexterity modifier damage.

entries.name: Alternatively
entries: You now gain a new natural weapon that you are proficient in, tongue lash. This tongue strike has the finesse property and a reach of 10 feet, dealing {@dice 1d6} + your Dexterity or Strength modifier in lewd or bludgeoning damage (your choice).
The reach on this natural weapon does not provoke opportunity attacks by leaving its reach unless you have at least one hand free.

feat.name: Living Shield
entries: Through masochistic preyish desires or dutiful pride, you have learned to become a living shield for your allies, saving allies from devourment or danger by taking their place. You gain the following abilities:

items: Upon a friendly creature within 10 feet of you being successfully {@condition grappled}, you may use your reaction to take their place. You become adjacent to both your friendly creature and the grappler, the friendly creature is no longer {@condition grappled}, and you instead become {@condition grappled}. If you are {@condition grappled}, {@condition restrained}, or otherwise unable to move, you are unable to use this ability.

Upon a friendly creature within 10 feet of you failing a devour contest check, you may use your reaction to quickly run over to them and take their place. You become adjacent to both your friendly creature and the grappler, the friendly creature is no engaged in a devour contest as you yank them out of the predator, and you instead become locked in a devour contest, with the predator gaining a number of successes equal to what they would have gotten on the prior target. If you {@condition grappled}, {@condition restrained}, or otherwise unable to move, you are unable to use this ability.
You gain resistance to non-magical digestion damage.

feat.name: Living Weapon
entries: Your body is a weapon: Your teeth are sharp, your body is strong, or perhaps you simply have such ample curves that you are able to smash them into your foes. Through these strengths, you are able to quickly change from punching, biting, and squishing foes to gulping them down. You gain the following effects:

items: Your body is now itself a weapon. This translates to gaining natural melee weapons you are proficient in and deal {@dice 1d6} + your Strength modifier damage. When you attack, you may choose if this damage is piercing, bludgeoning, slashing, or lewd damage.
Upon damaging an enemy with any melee attack, you may attempt a devour check as a bonus action without needing to have the target {@condition grappled}.

feat.name: Naturally Thick
entries: You are thicker and broader than most other creatures, or perhaps simply have a difficult body type or natural skills that make you more difficult to push around. With your increased curves also comes increased hunger and size… You gain the following effects:

items: You count as one size larger for the purpose of determining your capacity and base bulk.
Your weight is increased (GM and player discretion).
When you are the target of a {@action shove}, {@action grapple}, or {@action devour|lustvore}, you may use your reaction to gain advantage on the test.

feat.name: No Escape
entries: Your body is an inescapable prison of flesh. You gain the following effects:

items: When a {@condition swallowed|lustvore} creature succeeds on an escape attempt from within you, you can use your reaction to immediately attempt a devour check against them.
You gain advantage to resist any escape attempts from creatures inside you.

feat.name: Masseuse
entries: You're able to put the largest of predators at ease during rests, relaxing their joints and stretched guts. You gain the following effects:

items: When you take a short or long rest, you may spend some time doting on up to your Charisma modifier of creatures. Those creatures affected double their digestion speed during the rest, and gain temporary hit points equal to your level + {@skill Performance} modifier at the end of the rest.
Your massaging skills are quite excellent and give you advantage on {@skill Persuasion}, {@skill Deception}, {@skill Insight}, and other social checks while you are able to leverage your skills.
You gain the {@spell prestidigitation} and {@spell mending} cantrips.

Whenever you are wearing servant's clothing, you have an AC of 11 + your Charisma modifier. You may use a shield and still benefit from this AC. The servant's clothing may be freely flavored to fit your character.

When you take a long rest, you may designate a master. This master is a creature who you strive to assist in every way. As a reaction, whenever you master takes any kind of action that requires an attack roll or ability check, you may give them advantage on the roll so long as you are within 30 feet as you deftly assist them from the background. You may use this feature once per short rest.

feat.name: Mobile Predator
entries: Swallowing down prey barely even requires concentration at this point for you, allowing you to focus more on defending yourself from their vengeful allies, or on a hasty retreat with their legs still flailing from your lips. You gain the following effects:

items: When you are grappling a creature, you can move at full speed.
Your speed is no longer reduced to 0 when you are {@condition restained} while {@condition devouring|lustvore} a creature.

You no longer suffer the movement speed penalties for being {@condition restained} when over capacity or max capacity, although you still do suffer all other effects. While over max capacity, you move at ¼  your speed.

feat.name: Milkification
entries: You not only digest your prey, you are able to turn them into delicious milk, cum, or other liquid for others to consume! (this feat will use milk for its description, but is usable for any sort of liquid.

items: When you digest a meal, instead of gaining the normal benefits from digestion, you can instead turn them into milk. You gain an amount of milk equal to the bulk of all your digested food/prey in capacity points.

As an action, you can feed any number of capacity points worth of milk to an adjacent {@condition willing|lustvore} creature, or an unwilling one if they are {@condition grappled}. This milk heals 1 hit point per capacity, and is considered food as well.

As an attack, you may expend 1 or more points of milk up to your level to fire off a milk shot. This deals {@dice 1d6} + milk points of lewd damage, and the target must make a DC 10 + expended milk points Dexterity saving throw. On a failure, they are coated with milk. While coated, they are in difficult terrain and have disadvantage on Dexterity saving throws. A creature may use its action to wipe off the milk.

feat.name: Miniature Meatarian
entries: The smallest of the small, your hunger rivals that of predators thrice your size, as do your curves. Many predators have seen you as nothing more than a bite sized snack, only to find themselves made yours! You gain the following:

items: You are considered one size larger for the purposes of Capacity and Predator size.
You suffer no penalty to grappling against prey two sizes or more larger than yourself.

feat.name: Multiple Arms
entries: Generally, folks with multiple arms have a set of 4 arms total, but some may have even more than that. You gain the following effects:

items: You now have 2 additional arms and hands. These extra arms can manipulate an object, open or close a door or container, pick up or set down an object, or wield one weapon that has the light property in each.

You now can do an unarmed attack or lewd strike as a bonus action, but you do not gain your ability modifier to damage, unless that modifier is negative. You gain the ability modifier to damage if you gain the {@optfeature two-weapon fighting} style. The damage dice size for this bonus action unarmed attack stays at {@dice 1d4} no matter what other features say.

feat.name: Ogre's Belch
entries: Your belches are as powerful as an ogre's, bellowing out humid gusts of air that disrupt your enemies. As a bonus action, you can do one of the following:

items: You belch out a gust of powerful air. This is treated as a {@action shove}, except you can do it at a target up to 10 feet away.

You belch out a humid musky cloud. Choose a creature within 10 feet that you can see. They must make a Constitution saving throw DC 8 + your Proficiency Bonus + your Constitution modifier or be {@condition poisoned} until the end of their next turn.

Your belch sends an object inside of you flying, such as the bones of your digested meals. Make a ranged attack with 20/40 range that you are proficient in. On a hit, this attack deals {@dice 1d4} + Dexterity modifier bludgeoning, piercing, slashing, OR lewd damage depending on the nature of the object. When uncertain, ask your DM.

Your belch is a splitting cry, deafening those around you. All creatures within 10 feet must make a Constitution saving throw DC 8 + your Proficiency Bonus + your Constitution modifier or be {@condition deafened} until the end of your next turn.

feat.name: Predatory Confidence
entries: You are more than simply a predator, you are an alpha. One look from your steely gaze is all it takes to let anyone know you are not to be trifled with. Or perhaps, one look is all it takes to instill submission. You gain the following effects:

items: You gain proficiency in either {@skill Persuasion} or {@skill Intimidation}. If you are already proficient, you gain expertise in your chosen skill.

After swallowing a prey during your turn, as a free action you can extend out your predatory aura, letting all your potential prey know of their lovely or terrifying fate. Pick either frightening, or charming. All creatures of your choice within 15 feet must then make a Wisdom saving throw equal to 8 + your Charisma modifier + proficiency mod. On a failure, they are either {@condition frightened} or {@condition charmed} towards you for one minute depending on which aura you picked. At the end of its turn, an affected creature may make another save to shake off this effect. If they are {@condition charmed}, they are awestruck by your allure and may not move away from you, and may roll the test again if you or your allies do anything harmful to them, including {@condition devouring|lustvore}. You can use this ability once per short or long rest.

feat.name: Predatory Occupant
entries: You are not only used to being inside a belly, you know how to turn it to your predatory advantage, turning it into a symbiotic relationship. After all, with only one way in, all you need to do is open your mouth and wait.. You gain the following effects:

items: While {@condition swallowed|lustvore}, if another creature is fully {@condition swallowed|lustvore} into your same orifice, you may initiate a devour check as a reaction with advantage. On a success, you are able to gulp them down instantly. On a failure the prey manages to squirm their way away and is deposited into the stomach normally.

When you digest a meal, your predator gains the same effect for the digested meal. If you and your host predator have a separate capacity, calculate the digested meals capacity against the predator's capacity rather than your own for the predator's digestion benefits.

feat.name: Regurgitator
entries: You are quite accustomed to spitting out creatures and objects within your body, sometimes with devastating effect. You gain the following abilities:

items: You may now regurgitate creatures and objects as a bonus action, rather than an action.

In place of an attack, you may spit out a tiny size object or creature that was inside you. This is considered a ranged attack, has a range of 30/120, and deals {@dice 1d10} + Dexterity modifier damage. This damage is either bludgeoning, piercing, or slashing depending on the object. If this was a creature, on a hit the creature takes the same damage as the target.

feat.name: Semen Demon
entries: In olden lore, vampires were charming creatures that were known to lull their victims into a false sense of security and drink their blood. Though, there exists a breed of vampires that feed on more sensual fluids. You gain the following abilities:

items: When you suck on a {@condition charmed} or friendly creature, you can drain them over the course of one minute. You can gain 1 capacity point of sexual fluids and restore {@dice 1d6} + Charisma modifier hit points. You can do this up to half a creature's base bulk before you drain them completely, and cannot use this feature against them again until after their next long rest.

When you take the {@action grapple} or {@action devour|lustvore} action and it succeeds, you may declare to suck on the target's genitals as a bonus action. When you do, they take {@dice 1d6} + Charisma modifier in Lewd damage. You heal by half of the damage dealt. If they are reduced to 0 hit points by this, they are considered drained and gain a level of {@condition exhaustion}. They are also {@condition charmed} by you as they regard you with a lustful afterglow and are {@condition willing|lustvore} to be devoured (although not digested!)

feat.name: Sensational Touch
entries: Through your tongue, your body, your curves, or a breath, you are able to stun your opponents into sensual submission. You gain the following ability:

items: While grappling or in a devour contest with a creature (or one held in an otherwise compromising position where you can get at them with it), you can spend your action to force the target to make a Wisdom saving throw vs 8 + Charisma or Dexterity modifier + Proficiency Bonus or be overwhelmed with pleasure for 1 minute. During this effect, the 'victim' is {@condition charmed}. They regard you lustfully. This charm breaks if you or your companions do any non-lewd damage to the target or their allies, and they may roll the saving throw again whenever you deal lewd damage to the target.

If you spend 1 minute physically touching and physically flirting with someone, you can make a Charisma({@skill Performance}) check contested by the creature's Wisdom({@skill Insight}) check. If you or your companions are fighting the creature, your check automatically fails. If your check succeeds, the target is {@condition charmed} by you as long as it remains within 10 feet of you and for 1 minute thereafter, as they now regard you with sexual infatuation. This charm breaks if you or your companions take any hostile actions or deal damage to them or their companions.

feat.name: Shortstack Predator
entries: Although smaller than most, you are just as hungry as the biggest of them, and this shows in your voracious appetite and enhanced curves. You gain the following effects:

items: You are considered one size larger for the purposes of your capacity and devour checks where you are a predator.
Your bulk is increased by one size larger.
Whenever you attempt to devour a creature of a larger size than you, you may choose to gain advantage on the roll. You may use this ability once per short rest.

prerequisite.other: Small or tiny size, does not work if effectively permanently enlarged or similar.

feat.name: Silent Prey
entries: You have mastered an art of infiltrating predators and going unnoticed inside them to an inhuman degree.

items: For purposes of {@condition devouring|lustvore} or being devoured, you may choose to count as one size smaller whenever it benefits you.

When you are hidden from a creature you may attempt to crawl inside of them without their notice. As an action, you may attempt to force your way inside another creature of equal or larger size. If they are unwilling, roll an {@skill Athletics} or {@skill Acrobatics} contest vs their {@skill Athletics} or {@skill Acrobatics}. If you fail, your stealth is broken. If you succeed, you enter a devour contest with 1 success against the creature where you must achieve a number of successes equal to what a creature of their size would need to devour you. If they achieve a number of successes equal to yours then you fail the devour contest and your stealth is broken.

When feeding yourself to another, if you are more than 1 size smaller than the predator, you receive a +1 for each size category beyond that point. (If a tiny creature is slipping into a medium creature, they get a +1. Tiny into a large is a +2, etc)
A predator that is unaware of you cannot begin to digest you until they either eat something/someone else or you indicate your presence to them.
If you create noise or produce a bulge inside your predator, any observing creature has disadvantage to notice.

feat.name: Skull-collector
entries: Rather than keep the souls of your devoured prey in your body, you've instead learned to tie them to their skulls. You gain the following effects:

items: When you fully digest prey, you may belch up their skull whenever you choose. This skull acts as a magical object, and is possessed by the soul of the prey it belonged to.
The prey is bound to the skull until it is broken and is able to speak freely but cannot move.
There is no limit to how many skulls you can create and have active at a given time, unlike normal soul vore.

feat.name: Small
entries: Due to some quirk of heritage or of a magical nature, your body is unusually small for your race. Oftentimes, this turns you into a shortstack!

items: You permanently reduce your size down by one or more steps, up to a maximum size decrease of small, and you gain 10 feet to their walking speed up to a maximum of 40 feet including racial bonuses. Other effects can stack on top of this after like feats or class bonuses.
You gain one additional vore or lewd feat upon taking this feat.
Your decreased size may draw unwanted attention.

prerequisite.other: Medium or Larger size, Incompatible with the Large feat.

feat.name: Smotherer
entries: You are adept at using your body to smother your prey when you grapple.
As a bonus action, you can smother a creature you are grappling. The target is {@condition blinded} for as long as they remain {@condition grappled}.

feat.name: Soothing Stomach
entries: Your belly carries fortifying properties and can serve as a comfortable resting spot for the weary. You gain the following benefits:

items: When a creature completes a long rest spent entirely within your stomach, they gain temporary hit points equal to your level + your Constitution modifier. In addition, they regain all expended hit dice, and remove up to 3 levels of {@condition exhaustion}.
When a creature completes a short rest spent entirely within your body, they gain max rolls on hit dice spent for healing.
Any healing spells or effects (excluding hit dice) effecting prey inside your belly regain additional hit points equal to your Constitution modifier

feat.name: Soul Absorption
entries: You are able to trap your prey's soul and essence inside your body, and may reform them at a later time or simply torment them as part of your body fat. You gain the following abilities:

items: Upon fully absorbing a creature, you may declare to Soul Absorb them. In doing so you gain all the normal benefits of digestion. However, their soul is now trapped as part of your body. This must be marked in some physical and visible way upon your body. This could be a tattoo of them, tallymarks, tribal tattoo markings that cover more of your body the more prey there are, etc.

Soul absorbed prey cannot take any actions, speak, or do anything that might indicate their presence. However, they do retain their sentience, and generally feel whatever part of the body they have been ‘absorbed' into. Soul absorbed prey can telepathically communicate with other absorbed targets and you, if you allow them to.

You can reform any prey you have chosen to soul absorb. Upon consuming a meal of equal or greater capacity size to the original size of your soul absorbed prey, you can choose to reform one or more soul absorbed creatures during a long rest, with the total capacity of creatures reformed being under the total capacity of the meal. Upon being reformed, they are nude and have no equipment, and suffer 1 level of {@condition exhaustion}.

You can keep a number of soul absorbed prey equal to your Charisma modifier + your level. Should you ever exceed that amount, you must either release an absorbed creature's soul, or permanently absorb them. Upon permanent absorption you are no longer able to speak with them as their essence gradually and blissfully becomes one with yours. A creature absorbed this way cannot be revived through normal means except through exceptionally powerful magic such as wishes.

Should you ever die, your non-permanently absorbed targets souls are released. If you are reformed, they can willingly choose to return to your body. All permanently absorbed creatures always return, as they are part of you now.

During a long rest, you can focus your attention upon one of your soul absorbed prey and gain proficiency in one skill they are proficient in. You may gain one skill proficiency this way but can replace this with another long rest. You lose this benefit if they are ever reformed.

When you would be fully absorbed by a creature, you may optionally allow them to declare you as Soul Absorbed instead, following the above rules as long as they are {@condition willing|lustvore}. This only functions for you, and does not grant them the feat.

feat.name: Speedy Reformer
entries: Your body is able to more easily reform than most people, giving you the following bonuses:

items: Anytime you would be reformed from a long rest after having died by digestion, you may instead reform on a short rest.
Anytime an ability would require a meal of equal size, they instead require a meal of ½ your size to reform you.

Anytime an ability only allows reformation or revival within a certain time limit, that time is extended a number of months equal to your Charisma modifier. If this time limit is less than the one of the spell/effect, the time limit is unaffected.

feat.name: Stomach of Holding
entries: Perhaps due to a magical experiment, or simply your body adapting to your desires, you have somehow gained a second stomach pouch.

items: You gain a new space in your body known as your stomach of holding. When you swallow a creature or at the end of your turn before you deal digestion damage, you can push an object or a creature from your stomach into your stomach of holding. You can hold up to 500lbs. of inanimate objects or 8 capacity worth of creatures in your stomach of holding without counting towards your Capacity.
If you ever exceed your capacity, the heaviest object or creature in your stomach of holding is pushed into your normal stomach.
As a bonus action, you can pull any object out of your stomach of holding by regurgitating it (or pushing it out through another orifice!).

Regardless of what is in your stomach of holding, you may choose to appear as if you have nothing in your stomach, and it is impossible for people to detect anything you have inside your stomach of holding outside of extraordinary magical means that would allow them to see inside normal bags of holding.

feat.name: Stomach Squatter
entries: Some creatures have taken their love for residing in bellies to an extreme: They don't merely enjoy bellies, they practically live in them, and will fight any attempt to remove them from their comfortable home!

items: When you take a long rest inside a belly, you regain all of your hit dice rather than half.

Once per short rest, as an action you may choose to make yourself near impossible to digest. You gain immunity to all non-psychic digestion damage, so long as you do not take any type of actions/bonus actions/reactions. This state lasts until you take an action/bonus action/reaction. You may not rest in this state, nor gain benefits from rest.

When a predator attempts to regurgitate you and you do not wish to be spit out, they must roll a Constitution saving throw vs 8 + your Dexterity or Strength modifier + your Proficiency Bonus. On a failure, you remain in their belly. If they fail on their saving throw by 5 or more, they cannot attempt again for another 1 hour or until damaged by you as you wedge yourself deeper inside of them. These effects do not stop them from digesting you!

feat.name: Struggler
entries: You are an exceptionally strong struggler, and able to kick and punch in ways to make your predator more than uncomfortable. While inside a creature, you do not have disadvantage on skill checks. In addition, when you successfully take the struggle action, you may choose one additional effect from the following:

items: The next attack against the predator is made with advantage.
The next saving throw the predator rolls is made with a disadvantage until your next turn.
The next ability check the predator rolls is made with a disadvantage until your next turn.
The predator takes damage equal to {@dice 1d10} + your Strength modifier
The predator must make a {@status concentration} check at DC 8 + Strength modifier + Proficency Bonus. On a failure, they are poisoned until your next turn.

feat.name: Slick With Spit
entries: Your salivary glands work on overdrive. You gain the following effects:

items: Your spit is now exceptionally potent. You gain a new feature, spit, which is used by various abilities. While a creature is affected by your spit, all devour checks against them have advantage and all grapple tests against them have disadvantage.

Whenever a prey escapes from a devour contest where you had at least 1 success, or is otherwise regurgitated from being fully {@condition swallowed|lustvore} by you, they are covered in copious amounts of slick saliva or other juices for 1 minute. During this time they are affected by your spit, and at the end of their turn they must roll a Dexterity saving throw vs DC 8 + Constitution modifier + Proficency Bonus or your spell save DC, whichever is higher, or fall prone. They can use their action to wipe off the spit.

As an action, you can huck a spitball at a creature you can see within 30 feet. They must make a Dexterity saving throw vs DC 8 + Constitution modifier + Proficency Bonus or your spell save DC, whichever is higher, or be affected by your spit for 1 minute. They can use their action to wipe off the spit.

While you are grappling or {@condition devouring|lustvore} a creature, you may attempt to lick them as a bonus action. They must roll a Dexterity saving throw vs DC 8 + Constitution modifier + Proficency Bonus or your spell save DC, whichever is higher, or be affected by your spit until the end of your turn.

feat.name: Slow Digestion
entries: Your system is quite patient and slow at breaking down its prey. However, this makes it quite efficient. You gain the following effects:

items: Your digestion lasts 4 times as long as it normally would for a meal. While digesting, at least 1 capacity worth of creature, you do not require food or water. In addition, most prey generally last for many hours before fully expiring. When you put prey into the “digested” state to start processing, they hold on for 1/2 of your digestion time before technically expiring. During this time, should you be forced to regurgitate your prey, they will exit in a stable state.

Every long rest you take while you are digesting at least ½ your capacity, you restore all your hit dice rather than half, and you gain your Constitution modifier + your level of temporary hit points upon waking up.

feat.name: Swift Digestion
entries: Your system is fast at mushing and sucking up your prey when you can take the time to let your gut work. You gain the following effects:

items: So long as you are equal to or below capacity, you can finish digestion on a short rest.
If you are above capacity but not over your max capacity, digestion can be finished on a long rest.
Your time for digesting a max capacity meal is halved.

feat.name: Symbiotic Predator
entries: Your belly has learned to treat its prey as more than just a quick meal, instead gradually sapping nutrients while simultaneously curing their own hunger through a unique relationship.

items: While inside your body, your prey never needs to eat or drink.

You may choose to make any number of creatures inside you immune to your digestion as a free action, and may retract it just as easily. Gear does not count as part of a creature (and thus may be digested separately).
While you are filled with at least ½ your capacity's worth of living creatures, you are considered fed.

Once per short or long rest, when you have at least one creature inside of you, you can draw upon your prey for a surge of temporary strength as a free action. Doing so allows you to reroll any one attack roll or skill check during your turn.

feat.name: Symbiotic Prey
entries: You have a unique relationship with your predators, and are able to provide them with sustenance and keep yourself sustained for far longer than normal. While inside a creature, you gain the following effects:

items: The creature you are inside never needs to eat or drink.
While you are inside a creature, you don't need to eat or drink.
If you are inside a predator that is {@condition willing|lustvore} to allow it, you can make yourself immune to their digestion as a free action.

As a bonus action you can heal your predator's hit points for {@dice 1d10} + your Charisma modifier. This improves to ({@dice 2d10}) at 5th level, ({@dice 3d10}) at 10th level, ({@dice 4d10}) at 15th level, and ({@dice 5d10}) at 20th level. You may use this ability once per short rest.

feat.name: Tail Vore
entries: You have learned how to use your tail as an extension of your drive to consume. You gain the following effects:

items: If it did not already, your tail now counts as another orifice you can use to devour targets, and can be used as another hand for grappling.

As a bonus action, when your tail is not already {@condition devouring|lustvore} something, you can attempt to devour creatures with your tail even if they are not {@condition grappled}. This test is done with disadvantage if they are not {@condition grappled}, or normally if they are {@condition grappled}.

feat.name: Transformative Digestion
entries: You have learned how to successfully assimilate souls you devour into parts of your body directly. You gain the following effects:

items: After soul absorbing a creature, friend or foe, you may attempt to transform them into a part of yourself. Whichever part they become, they will have a somewhat 50/50 control over that part of you, and remain sentient and keep most of their intelligence.
When you release the creature's soul, the part returns to normal.

The creature added to you can only perform actions relative to its new position; a cock may be able to vore targets, while a tail might help you grapple or bludgeon enemies- likewise, someone added as simple fat can't do more than wobble.

After being Soul Absorbed by a creature, you may allow them to transform you into a part of themself following the above rules as long as they are {@condition willing|lustvore}. This only functions for you, and does not grant them the feat.

feat.name: Tough Gut
entries: Your gut might as well be lined with iron for how tough it is. You gain the following effects:

items: You gain resistance to all slashing, bludgeoning, and piercing damage done inside you.
You may use your reaction to gain advantage against any prey attempting to struggle.
You are immune to all negative effects of potions, poisons, food, and other digested materials.

feat.name: Voracious
entries: A skilled predator is quick in their consumption.
As a bonus action, you may make a {@action devour|lustvore} attack in the same turn you make a {@action grapple} attack.

Where there is civilization, there are almost certainly golems. Being tireless creations that require no food, sustenance, or rest, golems are often treated as a premium workforce. Where a man can do a job well, a golem can do it perfectly and consistently.

However, despite their usefulness, they come at an inherent risk. Over time, Golems inevitably begin to develop their own personalities, traits, desires, quirks, and even free will. In most cases, this is not a problem, and in fact rather a pleasant surprise. After all, due to their usually helpful nature, Golems naturally desire to assist where they can, and often become true members of the families and households they serve. However, this is not always the case, and sometimes it is difficult to spot until it's too late. The golemancers who often manage and repair them are often too biased towards their own creations to be used as good judges of character, and more than one golem has realized the individuals they serve are not worthy of their services, and begin to slowly twist and bend their commands to serve their own purposes…
{@b Golems and Adventurers:}

Free Golems are exceedingly rare in the world. More than once free golems have gone on murderous rampages against their former masters, or most terrifyingly, simply had no concept of why their actions were wrong at all. Thus, most that become free are often slain due to their logically warped consciousnesses. However, those golems that begin to learn and understand the world often desire to gather more data and experience “life” outside of their normal functions, and often choose to integrate with wandering parties and adventurers.

entries.name: Age
entries: Golems are constructed and animated, and do not age.

entries.name: Alignment
entries: Golems always are created lawful, as they obey their runic bindings to a fault. However, golems often slowly begin to develop quirks, a personality, and free will in the constraints of their bindings. Or in some rare cases of freed golems, complete free will. In the course of time, they may develop a wide variety of alignments.

entries.name: Size
entries: Golems are usually made in a similar image to their creators, and are usually between 5-6ft and medium size. However golems can be made of any size.

entries.name: Half-Construct
entries: You were created to have remarkable fortitude, represented by the following benefits:

items: You have advantage on saving throws against being {@condition poisoned}, and you have resistance to poison damage.
You don't need to eat, drink, or breathe.
You are immune to disease.
You don't need to sleep, and magic can't put you to sleep.

entries.name: Sentry's Rest
entries: When you take a long rest, you must spend at least six hours in an inactive, motionless state, rather than sleeping. In this state, you appear inert, but it doesn't render you {@condition unconscious}, and you can see and hear as normal.

entries.name: Hardy Construction
entries: Golems have a natural armor of 12 + Dexterity modifier.

entries.name: Languages
entries: A golem knows common and the language of its creator.

action.name: Devour
entries: When you want to swallow a creature, you can use the {@action Attack} action to make a Special melee Attack, a Devour. If you're able to make multiple attacks with the Attack action, this Attack replaces one of them. A creature must be {@condition grappled}, {@condition restrained}, or otherwise unable to move or have a moment speed of 0 to target them with this attack.

You must make a Strength({@skill Athletics}) or Dexterity({@skill Acrobatics}) check contested by the target's Strength({@skill Athletics}) or Dexterity({@skill Acrobatics}) check (the target chooses the ability to use). The prey may choose to be {@condition willing|lustvore} and automatically fail this test. If you succeed, you and the target enter a Devour Contest, and you gain a single success on the devour contest.

{@i Note: Like the {@action Grapple} and {@action Shove} actions, you can replace only one of your attacks that are part of your attack action with devour attacks. If you have multiple attack actions (such as fighter's action surge) you can replace one attack with a devour on both attack actions.}
{@b Devour Action and incapacitated creatures}

The devour action assumes you are attempting to devour unwilling and conscious creatures. If the creature is unable or unwilling to resist, you do not need to grapple them first in order to start a devour contest. To specify when this is commonly applicable:

You do not need to grapple creatures that automatically fail ability checks, or strength and dexterity saving throws in order to start a devour contest. This includes but is not limited to: {@condition blinded}, {@condition unconscious}, {@condition paralyzed}, {@condition petrified}, and {@condition stunned}.

action.name: Force-Feed
entries: You may try to force-feed yourself to another creature. As an {@action Attack}, when you are {@condition grappled} or grappling a creature, or in devour contest against another creature with you as prey, you may attempt to force yourself into the creature.

If they are unwilling, they may roll to resist the devour contest as if they were predator. On a success or if they are {@condition willing|LustVore}, the predator gains one devour success against you.

action.name: Rub
entries: All creatures now have access to the following attack, Rub.

You may only target rub against a creature with at least one or more creature inside of it. This attack automatically hits one creature inside the target creature and deals lewd or bludgeoning damage equal to:

condition.name: Defeated
entries: These rules purposefully contain many options to non-lethally subdue a foe. A live squirming prey to gulp down is far more interesting than a dead or unconscious one after all! For this purpose, a new incapacitated state is added: {@i The {@condition defeated|lustvore} State}.

When a foe is brought to 0 hit points by a player character through any means (including lewd damage, range damage, spells, and so forth) instead of being unconscious or killed, they may instead be put into the {@i Defeated} state. {@condition defeated|lustvore} foes follow all the same rules as being unconscious: They are {@condition incapacitated}, it drops whatever its holding and falls {@condition prone}, it fails its Dexterity and Strength checks, all attacks vs it gain advantage, and attacks within 5 feet are critical hits.

However, {@condition defeated|lustvore} foes are still considered conscious. They cannot move in any significant amount, but they can weakly speak and struggle until they regain 1 hit point. If left alone, they may be able to crawl at a rate of 5 feet per turn at DM's discretion.

condition.name: Devouring
entries: Also colloquially referred to as the “nomming” condition, this condition simply means you are in the process of {@condition devouring|lustvore} someone through a devour contest or being devoured by someone else. So long as you remain in a devour contest either as predator or prey, you suffer the following effects from the devour contest condition:

items: You are {@condition restrained}, and {@condition grappled} if you are prey.
You are locked into a devour contest, either as predator or prey. Keep track of successes per the {@condition devouring|lustvore} rules for both pred and prey.
The {@i lewded} condition lasts until the end of your next turn, though at your and the DM's discretion may last longer.
A {@i lewded} creature automatically fails any contested roll against the source of their lewding.
A {@i lewded} creature has disadvantage to all checks, saves, and attack rolls made until the condition ends.

Once after combat (with DM permission), a character who was {@i Lewded} may recover up to a third of their health rounded down. This recovery can only be done once regardless of how many times the condition is triggered, and if it is not taken after the combat is over the potential recovery is lost. This is usually flavored as a rush of energy following an exciting situation, but may be flavored as you like.

condition.name: Swallowed
entries: When a predator succeeds on a devour contest vs a creature, that creature gains the new {@i Swallowed} condition.

items: You have disadvantage on all skill checks.
You are {@condition restrained}.
You have total cover from outside effects and cannot see outside of the creature and stomach you are within.
You automatically move where a predator does and are considered to be in the predator's same square, and adjacent for the purposes of ranged attacks.

You must successfully make a {@status concentration} check vs the predator's stomach AC before casting a spell. If you fail, you do not cast the spell, but you do not lose the spell slot or other resource.
If you are concentrating on a spell and the creature your {@condition swallowed|lustvore} by takes damage, you must make a {@status concentration} check at DC 10 or ½ the damage, whichever is higher.

condition.name: Willing
entries: In these rules, there are many spells and effects that refer to a creatures “willingness” to be devoured. If a creature is {@i willing}, it means they are perfectly ok with being devoured by select creatures, likely due to thinking of them as trusted allies or lovers, and may have the new {@i Willing} condition upon them.

Outside of effects that specify a creature's willingness (often as part of charm effects), it is always the creature's right to decide if they are {@i willing} or {@i unwilling}. Generally, all creatures are considered to be {@i unwilling}, unless otherwise specified by them or an ability, and thus all normal vore rules apply to them.. This is also done on a case by case basis. A creature can be {@condition willing|lustvore} to be devoured by one predator, but not another.
